get.summary:
Which players of one game are true mains of the champion they are on —
the desktop app's mark on its loading screen and Game page (#1910). One
call per game: up to ten `player=Name#TAG:championId` pairs and the
game's platformId. Only the true mains come back; a
player who is not one, or whom TrueMain does not track, is absent.

parameters.name: platformId
parameters.description: The Riot platform the game is played on, e.g. `EUW1`.

parameters.name: player
parameters.description: Each player as `Name#TAG:championId`, at most ten.

get.summary:
Name/tag lookup for the search box: returns a short, ranked list of
truemains whose Riot id matches q (case-insensitive
substring on the game name; a `Name#TAG` query also narrows by
tag). Always 200 with a (possibly empty) list — a too-short or no-match
query is a normal empty result, not an error.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The search term: a partial game name, or a full `Name#TAG` Riot id.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Maximum results to return. Omitted or `0` means "use the default":
the service treats `limit <= 0` as its default page size — the
same 0-as-sentinel convention `GET /truemains` uses for
`pageSize` — and clamps values above its cap down to it.

parameters.name: Sort
parameters.description:
Ranking column, always descending: `dedication` ranks by TrueMain's
dedication score, `games` / `kda` / `winRate` by the
row's Games / KDA / WR figure (case-insensitive); anything else
(including omitted) keeps the default ranked-standing order.

get.summary:
Player-scoped champion page: the same ChampionResponse
contract as `GET /champions/{championId}`, but every aggregate is
computed only from this player's games on the champion. 404 when the
account is unknown or the player has no aggregated games on the champion;
a thin sample still renders (`ChampionsListOptions.MinPlayerBuildGames`
only steers which patch is picked).

Player-scoped lane matchups: the same ChampionMatchupsResponse
contract as `GET /champions/{championId}/matchups`, but every line is
computed only from this player's games on the champion, and with no games floor:
every opponent the player faced is listed, from one game up. position
is required — a role opponent is only meaningful within a position — but may be
`ALL`, which pairs each game with the opponent of the position the player
held in it and merges the lines by opponent champion. A missing or unrecognised
one is a 400; 404 when the account is unknown. opponent
narrows to a single head-to-head.

Player-scoped performance: TrueMain's per-match performance score
aggregated over this player's most recent ranked games on the champion,
with the per-component breakdown behind it. 400 for an unrecognised
position; 404 when the name tag is malformed or the account is unknown.
A known player with too thin a sample is a 200 carrying the counts and no
averages, so the page renders an honest "not enough games yet".

parameters.name: nameTag
parameters.description: The player's Riot id in `Name-TAG` route form.

parameters.name: championId
parameters.description: The champion to scope the sample to.

parameters.name: patch
parameters.description: Major.minor patch filter; omitted means every patch.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: Position filter; omitted or `ALL` means every position.

get.summary:
Activity grid under the profile's LP curve (#927, reshaped in #1473): the
player's ranked games drawn one square per UTC day, in three windows — every
day of the current patch, the last seven days, and today's games one square
each. 404 only when the name tag is malformed or the account is unknown.
get.description: The three windows ship in one response because they are foldings of the same participant rows, read once: switching window is a client-side toggle, which is what keeps two of them from disagreeing about the same afternoon. Every day inside a calendar window is emitted, played or not — an idle day carries `games: 0` and a null win rate, which is the wire-level difference between "did not queue" and "lost everything".

get.summary:
Full detail payload for a single match the player took part in: all 10
participants with their build order, skill order, rune page and the
timeline-derived laning stats. nameTag scopes the
route (the account must have played the match) but the response covers
every participant. 404 when the name tag is malformed, the account is
unknown, or the match id is not one this account played in.
Every known player with a tracked account, slug and last update — the sitemap's source (#2018).
The person behind slug: name, public links, accounts. 404 when unknown.

post.summary:
Bulk counterpart to `GET accounts/{nameTag}`: for each Riot ID, whether we already
    track it, whether it is still usable, and when we last ingested it. Nothing else.
    A POST because the input is a list, not because it writes — this is a read. It exists
so a batch caller stops looping the account explorer: that endpoint traces one Riot ID
through the entire pipeline, which is right for an operator and ruinous a few thousand
times in a row (the OTP seeder's first run drove it into 30-second timeouts on the live
site). Capped at int AccountFreshnessRequest.BatchLimit entries per request so
the query stays bounded; a caller with more sends several batches.
    400 for an entry missing a gameName/platformId, an unknown platform route, or a batch
    over the limit.

Seeds a single account into the pipeline by its Riot ID (gameName +
tagLine + platformId), instead of waiting for the ladder Discovery to
surface it. Records a `SeedRequest` at `Pending` and returns 202;
the Ingestor's ManualSeedProcess does the actual Riot resolution + account
upsert later. Idempotent: an existing unprocessed (Pending/Resolving)
request for the same Riot ID on the same platform is returned as-is rather
than duplicated (still a 202). 400 for a missing name/tag or an unknown
platform route.

get.summary:
Manual seed ("add a main") requests, newest-first, paged (#1166).
status is an exact `SeedRequestStatus` name
(case-insensitive; unknown values are ignored) and search is a
case-insensitive substring match on the Riot ID (gameName/tagLine).
get.description:
Paged rather than capped at a "recent" limit because the queue is no longer
operator-sized: one weekly OTP seeder run adds tens of thousands of requests, and a
list that can only show its newest page cannot answer how much is left to drain.
The response carries the filtered total for exactly that.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Restrict to a single `SeedRequestStatus` (Pending/Resolving/Ingested/Failed).
Omit for all.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Riot ID substring (gameName/tagLine). Omit for none.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: Restrict to one PlatformId (e.g. "EUW1"). Omit for all.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page index (backend clamps to ≥ 1).

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Rows per page (backend clamps to [1, 100], default 25).

get.summary:
Traces one Riot ID through the whole pipeline (#1032): identity and refresh
    state, the match-ingestion lease, the candidate funnel, the analysed main
    champions and the rank history, in one read-model. Read-only, and
    database-only — the API holds no Riot client, so this never resolves a Riot
    ID that the pipeline has not already recorded.
    Declared after the literal accounts/seed routes; literal segments
outrank the {nameTag} parameter, so those keep resolving to the seed
endpoints.

parameters.name: nameTag
parameters.description:
The Riot ID, either as typed (`Name#TAG`, percent-encoded) or in the
hyphen slug form the public routes use (`Name-TAG`). 400 when it parses
as neither.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description:
Restrict the search to one platform (e.g. "EUW1"). Omit to search every
region — a Riot ID is only unique within a routing region, so the read-model
lists any other account carrying it. 400 on an unknown platform, because
silently answering "never discovered" for a typo would be a lie.

get.summary:
Lists main candidates (the ingestion pipeline: New → Scored → Queued →
Processing → Validated), most-relevant first, paged. Filterable
by status and region (PlatformId), and
searchable by search over the joined Riot ID
(gameName/tagLine), PUUID, or — when numeric — champion id. Read-only.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Restrict to a single `MainCandidateStatus` (case-insensitive name:
new, scored, queued, processing, validated). Omit for all.

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: Restrict to one PlatformId (e.g. "EUW1"). Omit for all.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Riot ID / PUUID / champion-id search. Omit for none.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page index (backend clamps to ≥ 1).

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Rows per page (backend clamps to [1, 100], default 25).

get.summary:
Candidate funnel throughput per period (#1024): intake split by source, scored,
promoted, validated and demoted, from the recorded run summaries.
get.description:
Deliberately not derived from `main_candidates` row counts: retention prunes
stale candidates, so counting rows by status per past period under-reports every
bucket and increasingly so the further back it looks. Bounded by the
`process_runs` TTL, which the response reports. The validated series is
forward-only and reads null before the counter existed — never zero.

get.summary:
The candidate funnel's level per period (#1403): how many candidates sat in each
status at the end of each period, from the hourly snapshots.
get.description:
The companion of `candidates/funnel`, which measures the same funnel's flow.
Forward-only and never backfilled: periods before the first snapshot are absent
from the series, never zero, because the level then was unmeasured rather than
empty — and unlike a counter, it cannot be reconstructed afterwards
(`main_candidates` has no `QueuedAtUtc`, and pruning deletes rows).

get.summary:
Queue latency for the candidates currently retained (#1024): median and p90 of
discovery → scoring and scoring → validated.
get.description:
A snapshot over the rows that exist right now, not a historical average, and it
takes no window for that reason — pruned candidates are simply not in it. The
companion of `candidates/funnel`, which is the historical half.

get.summary:
Detail for one candidate: its pipeline fields + timestamps, the joined
account identity, the count of ingested matches for its PUUID, and the
linked manual seed request (matched on ResolvedPuuid + platform) when one
exists. 404 if no such candidate.

What every host is actually running with (#1034): the Api's own options, read live
from its container, plus the Ingestor's — published to Mongo at its own boot, since
the Api cannot introspect a process it does not run in. Read-only; no secret-bearing
section is ever included (see EffectiveConfigurationCatalog).

Storage growth over the last windowDays days plus the
disk-exhaustion forecast (#925), read entirely from the daily snapshots — this
endpoint never scans `pg_catalog` itself, unlike `db/tables` above.
Returns an empty model (not 404) before the snapshot step has ever run.

The automated anomaly detectors (#924): one card per detector with its
green/amber/red verdict, headline number, drill-down rows and the configured
thresholds it judged against. A detector that cannot measure reports
`unknown` — never green — rather than failing the panel.

Per-champion aggregate freshness on the newest patches, stalest first. Split off
the detector payload because it is the one measurement needing a grouped scan of
`champion_aggregate_scopes` — affordable on an explicit click, not on every
page view.

Lists matches flagged by the data-quality checks, grouped by issue type and
paged. Each check is queue-scoped so non-applicable rules (e.g. lanes on
ARAM) don't flood the panel. Read-only diagnostics — no repair.

parameters.name: issue
parameters.description:
Restrict to a single check (case-insensitive name: missingTimeline,
wrongParticipantCount, missingTeamPosition, zeroDuration, duplicateChampion).
Omit for all checks.

parameters.name: queue
parameters.description: Restrict to one queue id (e.g. 420). Omit for all queues.

parameters.name: minAgeHours
parameters.description: Only consider matches at least this many hours old.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page index for each issue group's sample.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Per-issue sample size (backend clamps to [1, 100], default 25).

get.summary:
Per-match data-quality detail: both teams laid out by position with the
gaps identified, plus the issue types the match trips. 404 if no such match.

The version changes of every Api and Ingestor container in the window, oldest first. A
restart on the same version is not a deploy and is not listed.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Window start (ISO 8601). Defaults to 30 days before to.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Window end (ISO 8601). Defaults to now.

get.summary:
Downloads and usage over the last windowDays UTC days, today included
(default 30, clamped to [1, 90]). Active installs today / 7 d / 30 d are read whatever
the window.

One page of persisted diagnostic logs, newest-first. level
is a minimum-severity threshold; category a
case-insensitive prefix; search a case-insensitive
substring over message/exception; eventType and
process case-insensitive exact matches on the ops-event
name and the producing host ("Api"/"Ingestor"); hasException
true restricts to rows carrying a formatted exception.

One page of recorded process crashes, newest-first. Each row carries the full
report (exception chain, environment + memory/GC snapshot, and the last log
lines before the crash), so the admin Crashes panel needs no separate detail
call. process ("Api"/"Ingestor") and source
(a `CrashSource` name, case-insensitive) are exact filters;
search matches message/stack-trace case-insensitively;
since is a lower bound on the crash time.

One page of the operator-action trail (#2288), newest-first. action,
targetType, targetId and actor are
exact filters; since (inclusive) and until (exclusive)
bound the time; search matches any metadata value case-insensitively.

post.summary: Starts a run of an external process. 400 for a name the API does not accept.

get.summary:
One page of recorded process runs, newest first, plus the per-process
rollup (computed over the full filtered set, unaffected by paging).

parameters.name: processName
parameters.description: Restrict to a single process. Omit for all.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: A `ProcessRunStatus` name (case-insensitive). Omit for all.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description:
Lower bound on `StartedAtUtc`; also the rollup's in-window cutoff. Omit
for no time floor, in which case the rollup's in-window counts are true
all-time totals (no hidden default window).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Legacy page size, kept for backward compatibility: honoured as
pageSize when that param is absent, superseded by it
otherwise. Prefer pageSize.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page index (backend clamps to ≥ 1).

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Rows per page (backend clamps to [1, 500], default 100).

post.summary:
Keeps a Running run alive and, when a summary is sent, replaces it. 404 for an unknown
run or one that is not an external process's; 409 once the run is finished.

Finishes a Running run as Success, Failed or Cancelled, with its error and final
summary. 404 for an unknown or non-external run; 409 when it is already finished.

get.summary: The alerter's settings, open incidents and newest alerts.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Alerts to return, newest first: 10 by default, at most 50.

get.summary:
Whether the patches the public surfaces read are actually servable (#1033): per
     patch, matches and participants ingested by game date, how many
     `(champion, lane)` lines have an aggregate at all and how many clear the
     games floor the champion directory reads with, which lines are still below it, and
     each fold's coverage and freshness on that patch.

     Its own endpoint rather than a card on the aggregation panel because it is a set of
grouped scans over tables that carry no index on their patch column — affordable
behind an explicit navigation, not on a page that loads on login.
Open channel conflicts, the most channels in common first, paged.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Substring of either persona's slug or name.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page (clamped to ≥ 1).

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Conflicts per page (clamped to [1, 100], default 25).

get.summary:
The open conflicts a bulk merge at minScore would settle: a shared social
channel, no differing one, a score at the floor. At most int PersonaConflictBulk.BatchLimit.

parameters.name: minScore
parameters.description: The score floor, at least 10 (one shared social channel).

post.summary:
Merges the listed conflicts, each into its older known player, after checking again that it is
open, lists no differing channel and still reaches `minScore`. One outcome per id; a
conflict that no longer qualifies is skipped with its reason, never failing the batch.

get.summary: Known players, most recently updated first, paged.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: `All` (default: live ones), `Conflicts`, `Unresolved` or `Removed`.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: The source that first published the persona.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Substring of the slug, the name or a listed Riot ID's game name.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page (clamped to ≥ 1).

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Rows per page (clamped to [1, 100], default 25).

post.summary:
Adds a known player by hand. Accounts go through the intake's rules (resolved, seeded, or
recorded as a conflict) and are answered one by one. 409 when the slug was ever used.

get.summary: One known player in full: accounts and links with their source, exclusions, open conflicts.

patch.summary: Renames a known player; the sources no longer overwrite the name.

delete.summary:
Removes a known player: no page, and the scrapers cannot recreate it. takedown
also bars its accounts from every other persona.

post.summary: Adds a link by hand (source `manual`). 409 when the persona already lists it.

delete.summary: Removes a link; the sources can no longer add it back.

post.summary:
Adds an account by hand, answered with its intake status (`linked`, `seeded`,
`conflict`, `excluded` by a takedown, …).

delete.summary: Unlinks an account; the persona's sources can no longer link it back.

post.summary:
Settles as merges the open conflicts whose two known players have the same name, into the
older of the two. The intake runs the same sweep after every batch; this one is the backlog's.

get.summary: Groups of live known players sharing a name, in name order, paged.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Substring of a name or slug in the group.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page (clamped to ≥ 1).

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Groups per page (clamped to [1, 100], default 25).

post.summary: Merges known players into the one kept: their slugs redirect to it. 409 when one is no longer live.
Marks known players as different people: their group leaves the queue. 409 when one is no longer live.

Upserts up to int PersonaBatchRequest.BatchLimit personas, each keyed on its slug,
and answers one result per persona in request order. A malformed persona is reported in its
result and skipped, never failing the batch; 400 only for a batch over the limit.

get.summary:
Accounts two personas claim, most recently seen first, paged. Every filter is optional; an
unknown status, source or region is a 400 rather than an empty page.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: `Open` or `Resolved`; omit for both.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: The source of the claim (`Dpm`, `Leaguepedia`, …).

parameters.name: region
parameters.description: A platform id (`EUW1`).

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Substring of either persona's slug or name, or of the Riot ID.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page (clamped to ≥ 1).

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Rows per page (clamped to [1, 100], default 25).

get.summary: One conflict with both personas in full — every account and link, with its source.

post.summary:
Settles an open conflict: `move` the account to the claiming persona, `keep` it with
its holder, `detach` it from both, or `merge` the two personas (`keep`: which one
stays). The decision holds against the scrapers' next runs. 409 when the conflict is already
resolved or the account changed hands since.

get.summary:
Recent pipeline iterations for the admin chain view: one full pass of the
ingestor pipeline per iteration, newest first, each carrying its ordered
process runs (status / duration / summary). Only iteration-stamped runs are
grouped; historical un-grouped rows are surfaced through
`GET /ops/process-runs` instead.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1-based page index (backend clamps to ≥ 1).

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: Iterations per page (backend clamps to [1, 50], default 10).

parameters.name: finishedOnly
parameters.description:
When true, excludes the in-flight iteration from both the page and the total
so a completed-history list paginates correctly. Default false.

parameters.name: lane
parameters.description:
`fetch` or `aggregate`: only the passes that ran that lane (a `Full` pass
counts for both). Omit, or pass anything else, for every pass.

get.summary:
The pipeline the ingestor runs: its steps in order, with their lane, label and
description, and the lanes that partition them.

Per ops route over the window: request count, p50/p95 (estimated from fixed buckets),
mean, max, timeouts and 5xx, and a p95 sparkline — slowest p95 first.

parameters.name: window
parameters.description: Relative window: `24h` (default) or `7d`.

get.summary: Matches-over-time histogram, bucketed by game date (`Match.GameStartTimeUtc`) at the requested granularity and returned chronologically. For day/week/month/year each bucket key is the ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the truncated period start; for patch it is the normalised "MAJOR.MINOR" version (ordered by the earliest game per patch, so it sorts chronologically rather than lexically). region is an optional `PlatformId` filter. 400 if granularity is missing or not one of day|week|month|year|patch.

Match ingestion throughput: how many matches the pipeline actually ingested
per period, from the recorded `MatchIngestion` run summaries (#1025).
get.description: Not a variant of `stats/matches-over-time`, which buckets games by when they were played and barely moves when ingestion stalls. This one answers whether the pipeline kept up. Bounded by the `process_runs` TTL, which the response reports so the caller can state the bound rather than drawing the tail beyond it as zero ingestion.

get.summary:
Aggregation pipelines snapshot for the admin Aggregation panel: per family
(builds patterns, matchups, synergies, mains) the planner's row estimates
of its tables, its champion coverage and the latest recorded run, plus the
ingestion backlogs that should read zero when aggregations are caught up.
Served from a two-minute cache (#2303).

Riot API usage metrics for the admin panel (#93): call counts per endpoint,
status-code breakdown, a bucketed call-volume series and the latest
rate-limit header snapshot, over a relative window.

parameters.name: window
parameters.description: Relative window: `1h`, `24h` (default), `7d` or `30d`.

parameters.name: endpoint
parameters.description: Optional exact endpoint key (e.g. `match-v5.match`) to restrict to.

get.summary:
Riot quota utilisation per routing host (#1458): each host's measured call rate
against the app limit it advertised, its 429 rate and the caller × endpoint pairs
spending it, plus the duty cycle of each ingestor lane over the same window.

parameters.name: window
parameters.description: Relative window: `1h`, `24h` (default), `7d` or `30d`.

get.summary:
The Ingestor's own meter (#1636): run failures, Riot rate-limit waits and 429s, each
instrument split by tag set and summed over the window from the per-minute rollups its
meter exporter writes.

parameters.name: window
parameters.description: Relative window: `1h`, `24h` (default), `7d` or `30d`.

get.summary:
The region's Grandmaster and Challenger thresholds, one entry per measured UTC day
(#2174): the lowest LP in each league that day, which the ranked card's LP curve draws
as the line where those tiers begin. Days before the first measurement are absent.

parameters.name: platformId
parameters.description: The Riot platform, e.g. `EUW1`.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: The window, in days back from today (90 by default, 730 at most).

get.summary: The shop classes of every classed item of the patch.

parameters.name: patch
parameters.description: Optional, as Data Dragon names it (`16.20.1`); the newest published data when omitted.

post.summary:
Build recommendation for a (possibly partial) draft: the player's
champion (route) and position plus the known ally/enemy picks. The
composition ranks historical games, it never hard-filters — a sparse
draft degrades to the champion's recent games at the position and the
confidence block says so. POST because the input — up to nine
champion/position slots — is too rich for query parameters. With a
`player`, only that player's games are sampled; 404 when we hold no
such account.

The games the recommendation for that same draft was computed from, one
page at a time, in the selection's own order (mains first, then
similarity, recency breaking ties). Same body as the recommendation
itself — the draft is the identity of the selection — so the two always
answer about the same sample; a separate route because the matchup page
refetches the build on every draft edit and must not pay for hydrating
match rows nobody opened (#940).

get.summary:
The damage profile of every champion the profile snapshot resolves for the patch, its
split by build archetype, and a static class for the champions it does not.

parameters.name: patch
parameters.description: Optional; the newest profiled patch when omitted.

get.summary:
One page of the directory (#1734): the same `(champion, position)` lines as
`GET /champions`, narrowed to a lane and/or a champion, ordered by
query's `sort`/`order` (pick rate, descending, by
default) and paged, with the filtered total and the resolved patch. The listing page
reads this so it never downloads the whole directory; the bare array above stays for
the consumers that do want every line (the OG card, the sitemap). A bad patch-free
filter (lane, elo) is a 400 as elsewhere; an unknown sort or order falls back to the
default rather than failing. "directory" is not an int, so the route never collides
with `{championId:int}`.

parameters.name: TruemainsOnly
parameters.description: Mains only (the default) or every tracked player with games on the champion.

parameters.name: Sort
parameters.description: `pickRate` (default), `winRate`, `banRate`, `games` or `tier`.

parameters.name: Order
parameters.description: `desc` (default, strongest first) or `asc`.

get.summary:
Champion meta / tier-list for a patch: `(champion, position)` rows
bucketed into S/A/B/C/D by a winRate + pickRate blend, tiered
independently per position. patch defaults to the
active patch; position narrows to a single lane when
set (an unrecognised position is a 400). Always 200 with a (possibly
empty) set of tier groups, all metrics derived from the same aggregates
the directory reads. The static route segment never collides with the
`{championId:int}` route below — "tierlist" is not an int.

Homepage-sized snapshot (#972): the active patch's true "games analyzed"
total (every aggregated game, not just the rows the ranked directory
keeps) plus a short, pre-sorted slice of its strongest rows. Always the
active patch, unfiltered — the homepage has no patch or elo picker of
its own. limit is clamped to `[1, 20]`, default
8. Reads the same cached entry as an unqualified `GET /champions`,
so the two never disagree and the homepage never pays for a second
aggregate computation. The static route segment never collides with the
`{championId:int}` route below — "overview" is not an int.

Winrate / pickrate evolution across the last five patches for a champion
on a single position. Intentionally cross-patch — it takes no patch
filter, so the directory's active patch never scopes the series. Read from
the light per-patch record (#1957), which honours the optional
eloBracket filter (a bad one is a 400 as elsewhere). Always
200 with a (possibly empty) series so the chart can render its own "not
enough data" state — a champion the directory never observed simply
yields no points.

post.summary: Resolve the enemy lanes and rank the candidate picks for one draft.

Suggest the bans for one draft: the threats to the player's declared pick,
or to their pool, never a champion an ally is playing (#1906).

get.summary:
The situational build context of a champion at a position (#1450): for every item
     its builds reach, whether it is core, situational or a preference, and — when
     situational — the draft situations that measurably move it, each with its rates and
     its sample.

     Deliberately narrower than its neighbours. There is no eloBracket and no
truemainsOnly: the verdicts carry no rank dimension (a situation is far rarer
than a champion, and splitting the games eleven ways starves the buckets the whole
feature rests on), so either parameter would be a filter that silently does nothing.
The response carries allRanks so the client can say so instead. There is no
opponentChampionId either: a matchup answers a different question from a
situation, and the verdicts are not folded per opponent.

     patch is optional — omitted, the newest patch this champion has
verdicts for is served, so a page whose patch filter has not settled still gets an
answer. A slice with no verdicts yet returns an empty list, not a 404: nothing
measured is a state, not an error.

Head-to-head between a Riot account and this champion's mains (issue
     #528): win rate, KDA, CS/min and gold side by side over the same queue,
     patch and lane scope. account is the Riot ID as a
     player types it (`Name#TAG`; the `Name-TAG` slug is accepted
     too) and is required. main narrows the right-hand
     column to a single tracked account; omitted, it aggregates every tracked
     main of the champion.

     Two distinct failure modes, deliberately kept apart:
     * A Riot ID that isn't well-formed — missing, blank, no separator,
     an empty half, over-long — is a 400. It is malformed input, not
     an answer about a player.
* A well-formed Riot ID we have no row for is a 200 carrying
     UNKNOWN_ACCOUNT (or UNKNOWN_TARGET for
     ). The comparison only covers accounts already in
     our database — there is no on-demand Riot fetch — so "we don't hold this
     player" is a normal answer for this endpoint, not a failure.

     A sample below the configured floor comes back as
     `INSUFFICIENT_SAMPLE` with both columns still populated so the
     caller can say which side is thin.

Lane matchups for a champion at a position: every lane opponent it met
(above the configured minimum-games floor) with its head-to-head game
count, win count and win rate, computed live from
`match_participants`. position is the required
Riot team position; an unrecognised position is a 400. Always 200 with a
(possibly empty) list — a champion with no opponent above the floor just
yields no entries. With opponent set, only that single
head-to-head is returned and the floor drops to one game (a deliberate
lookup); otherwise the frontend slices the best / worst from the list.

post.summary:
Rank the items this game's champion could complete next, from where its build stands
and against the game it is in.

get.summary:
How a champion's win rate scales with game length at a position: win rate
bucketed by game duration plus a single scaling index (long-game win rate
minus short-game win rate; positive = scales late), computed live from
match participants. position is the required Riot team
position; an unrecognised position is a 400. Always 200 with a (possibly
empty) bucket list — buckets below the sample floor are dropped.

Best duo partners for a champion at a position: for every teammate it has
been paired with often enough, the shared game count, the pair's win rate
and — the value the list is ranked by — the synergy, i.e. how far that win
rate lands above or below what the two champions' individual win rates
already predicted. position is the required Riot team
position and partnerPosition an optional narrowing to a
single partner lane; an unrecognised value for either is a 400. Always 200
with a (possibly empty) list — a champion whose own sample is too thin for
an expected win rate returns no entries rather than invented ones, and the
echoed `minGames` / `championGames` say why.

Third picks for an already-chosen duo: restricted to the games this champion
and partner actually played together, the teammates whose
trio over- or under-performed what all three individual win rates predicted.
position, partner and
partnerPosition are all required; an unrecognised position
is a 400. Always 200 — an empty completion list is the normal answer for a
duo too rarely played to split a third way, and the response carries the
duo's own game count so the caller can say exactly that.

Per tier and whole minute, the quartiles of a laner's cumulative CS and gold earned at
position, pooled over the newest patches. A minute under the sample
floor carries its count without quartiles. An unrecognised position is a 400.

Per tier, the quartiles of a laner's end-of-game KDA, kill participation, CS/min,
deaths and vision/min at position, pooled over the newest patches.
A tier under the sample floor carries its count without quartiles. An unrecognised
position is a 400.

AccountExplorerAccountRefReadModel.description: One of the other accounts sharing this Riot ID.

source.description:
The `MainCandidateSource` name. Note that `ManualSeed` is never
assigned in production — `ManualSeedProcess` reuses the ladder
upsert, so a manually seeded candidate reads `Ladder`. Read
SeedRequestReadModel? AccountExplorerReadModel.SeedRequest for the manual trail.

scoreInputs.description: The persisted inputs the score was computed from. The score's components are not stored — only the final blend is — so they cannot be shown. Recomputing them here would mix today's champion-scarcity snapshot into a number produced against an older one, and would silently disagree with double AccountExplorerCandidateReadModel.Score.

AccountExplorerCandidateReadModel.description:
One `main_candidates` row: where it sits in the
New→Scored→Queued→Processing→Validated funnel, and what the scorer saw.

lastPlayTimeUtc.description: Mastery `lastPlayTime` (ladder) or last observed game (harvest) — the recency input.

championRankInMasteryTop.description: Rank of this champion in the account's mastery top-N; 0 for harvest candidates.

observedGames.description: Games observed in orphan participant rows; 0 for ladder candidates.

observedWins.description: Wins among int AccountExplorerCandidateScoreInputsReadModel.ObservedGames. Persisted but not a scoring input yet.

AccountExplorerCandidateScoreInputsReadM.description:
What `ScoringProcess` had to work with. Ladder candidates carry mastery
rank/points; harvest candidates carry observed games/wins instead and leave
the mastery fields at zero.

confirmedByActivityCheckAtUtc.description:
The account's last successful mastery check. Deactivation is only
trustworthy alongside this: a failed lookup leaves both the flag and the
stamp untouched, so a null here means the retirement was never confirmed
by a completed check.

reasonKnown.description:
Always false: there is no retirement-reason column.
`MainActivityProcess` writes the boolean and nothing else.

reasonNote.description: The two causes the boolean collapses together, spelled out.

AccountExplorerDeactivationReadModel.description:
What is knowable about a deactivated main row — which is less than one would
like, and this record says so rather than guessing.

lastProfileSyncAtUtc.description: Last successful account-v1 identity resolution by `AccountRefresh`.

lastRankSyncAtUtc.description:
Last successful league-v4 read. Stamped even when the rank was unchanged
(no snapshot row written), so it is a freshness stamp, not a change log.

lastMainCalcAtUtc.description:
Last time `MainAnalysis` ran on this account. Can be newer than every
row's `CalculatedAtUtc` — see
bool AccountExplorerMainRowReadModel.AnalysisSkipped.

lastActivityCheckAtUtc.description: Last successful champion-mastery check by `MainActivity`. A failed lookup leaves this untouched on purpose, which is what makes it a usable "the retirement below was confirmed" marker.

lastMatchIngestAtUtc.description: Last completed match-ingestion pass over this account.

rankScore.description:
Denormalised rank sort key (tier/division/LP) from the latest snapshot.
Null when the account has never been seen ranked — not zero.

AccountExplorerIdentityReadModel.description:
The resolved account's identity and the per-process freshness stamps that say
when each half of the pipeline last touched it.

totalMatches.description: Matches the analysis pass looked at (its sample size), not the account's total.

isExtendedSample.description:
A main only thanks to the coverage-relaxed floor: its play rate sits below
the base threshold (#407).

analysisSkipped.description:
True when the account's last `MainAnalysis` run is newer than this
row's own `CalculatedAtUtc`: the process looked at the account and
declined to overwrite — the thin-sample guard (#825). Not a stale-data bug.

oneOf.description: Null while the row is active.

rows.description: Rows for the account, highest play rate first.

AccountExplorerMainsReadModel.description: The main-champion rows and the thresholds that decided them.

playRateThreshold.description: Base play rate required to be a main for a well-covered champion (0.20).

playRateFloor.description:
Lowest the adaptive threshold can drop to, for a maximally under-covered
champion (0.12, #407).

minMatchesToEvaluate.description:
Below this many analysed matches, `MainAnalysis` refuses to overwrite
an account that already has an established main (#825).

effectiveThresholdNote.description:
Why only a band is given: the effective per-champion threshold interpolates
between the floor and the base threshold according to a live
champion-coverage snapshot that is computed inside the Ingestor and never
persisted. Naming an exact number here would be an invention.

AccountExplorerMainThresholdsReadModel.description:
The configured `MainAnalysis` thresholds, so a row's verdict can be read
against the rule that produced it.

liveParticipantCount.description: Live `match_participants` rows for the PUUID: every champion, every queue, but bounded by retention (matches outside the retained patch window are hard-deleted).

oldestRetainedGameStartUtc.description:
Start of the surviving window, measured off the rows themselves rather
than derived from the retention config. Null when nothing survives.

newestRetainedGameStartUtc.description: End of the surviving window. Null when nothing survives.

careerGamesFromAggregates.description: Career games summed from the frozen `champion_aggregate_scopes`, which retention never deletes — but the aggregation only ever folded main champions, so this is not the account's whole history either.

aggregatedPatchCount.description: Distinct patches covered by those frozen scopes.

oldestAggregatedGameStartUtc.description:
Oldest `LastGameStartTimeUtc` across the scopes — a lower bound on how
far the frozen history reaches, since a scope records only its most recent
game, not its first.

lastAnalysisSampleSize.description:
Sample size of the most recent `MainAnalysis` pass, capped by
`MainAnalysis:MatchesToConsider` (50). A ceiling, not a total.

pruned.description: True when the frozen aggregates prove games existed that the live participant rows no longer hold. False does not mean nothing was pruned — the aggregates only cover main champions, so off-main games can be deleted without leaving any trace to detect.

prunedNote.description: The sentence explaining bool AccountExplorerMatchesIngestedReadModel.Pruned either way.

AccountExplorerMatchesIngestedReadModel.description:
How many games the pipeline holds for this account. Three different numbers
exist and they are not interchangeable — each is reported with the population
it counts, because presenting any one of them as "games" is how the
retention-asymmetry trap (#927) gets sprung.

AccountExplorerPositionStatReadModel.description: One lane of a main row's position breakdown.

region.description: The requested platform id (e.g. "EUW1"), or null when the search was region-wide.

AccountExplorerQueryReadModel.description: The request as the service resolved it.

wins.description: Queue totals from league-v4; null on snapshots taken before they were recorded.

query.description: The Riot ID and region the answer was resolved for, echoed back.

state.description:
One-word verdict, resolved first-match-wins so a player always lands in
exactly one state. See AccountPipelineState for the ladder
and what each value means. The booleans behind it stay exposed in the
sections below — the state is a headline, not the source of truth.

stateDetail.description:
The state in a sentence, built server-side so every consumer explains a
given state identically.

oneOf.description: Null when no `riot_accounts` row matches the Riot ID.

otherAccountsWithSameRiotId.description: The other accounts carrying the same Riot ID. `(GameName, TagLine, PlatformId)` is deliberately not unique — Riot IDs are recyclable and can collide across regions — so the resolver picks the most recently active row and lists the rest here rather than arbitrating in silence. Empty in the normal single-account case.

oneOf.description: Null when there is no account row to track.
Null when there is no account row to count games for.

candidates.description:
The account's `main_candidates` rows, highest score first. Always
empty when AccountExplorerIdentityReadModel? AccountExplorerReadModel.Identity is null: candidates are keyed on
`(PlatformId, Puuid)` and carry no Riot ID of their own, so a
candidate whose account has not been upserted yet is unreachable from a
Riot ID search.

oneOf.description:
The manual "add a main" request behind this account, if any — the only
reliable manual-seed signal (see
MainCandidateSource AccountExplorerCandidateReadModel.Source). Matched on the
resolved PUUID + platform when the account exists, and on the Riot ID
text when it does not — which is how a seed that never resolved is still
visible.

mains.description: The `main_champion_stats` rows plus the thresholds that judged them.

rankSnapshots.description:
Rank snapshots, most recent first, capped at
`AccountExplorerPanelReads.RankSnapshotCap`. At most one row per
UTC day, solo queue only, and never pruned by retention — so this is the
one series whose gaps really are gaps in play, not in storage.

AccountExplorerReadModel.description:
Everything the pipeline knows about one Riot ID, for the admin account
    explorer (#1032): identity, tracking/lease state, the candidate funnel, the
    main-champion rows and the rank history, in one read.
    The endpoint answers "why does this player not show up on the site?", so its
contract is that no state is ever inferred from an absent row without
saying so. An unknown Riot ID is a 200 with AccountPipelineState AccountExplorerReadModel.State =
NeverDiscovered, never a 404 — "we have never seen this account" is an
answer, not an error. Counts each carry the population they count, and the
retention-bounded ones carry the window they were measured over.
    Read-only, and deliberately database-only: the API holds no Riot client, so
this read cannot (and does not claim to) tell "never discovered" apart from
"this Riot ID does not exist at Riot".

isTracked.description:
True when the account satisfies either membership arm of the ingest claim.
There is no `IsTracked` column — this is derived, exactly as
`ClaimAccountsForMatchIngestAtomicallyAsync` derives it.

oneOf.description:
Which arm: "EstablishedMain", "QueuedCandidate", "Both", or null when
neither — i.e. the account is never selected for ingestion.

hasQueuedCandidate.description:
True when a candidate sits at `Queued`. It is the claim's new-candidate arm only
while the account was never ingested (#1535) — AccountTrackingArm? AccountExplorerTrackingReadModel.TrackedVia applies that rule.

matchIngestClaimedAtUtc.description: When the current lease was taken; null while Idle.

claimAgeSeconds.description:
Age of the current claim. Compare against the Ingestor's
`MatchIngestion:ClaimLeaseMinutes` (30 by default) to judge whether a
run died holding the lease — the API does not make that call for you.

neverIngested.description:
True when DateTime? AccountExplorerTrackingReadModel.LastMatchIngestAtUtc is null: the account has been
claimable but its lease has never come up. Never-ingested accounts sort
first in the claim query, so this plus a tracked flag means the queue has
not drained that far yet.

AccountExplorerTrackingReadModel.description:
Whether the account is in the match-ingestion population, and where its lease
    currently stands.
    Every threshold that would turn these numbers into a verdict — the claim
lease, the inactivity window, the retained patch count — is Ingestor
configuration the API cannot see. So this section reports timestamps and ages
and stops there; it never claims a lease is "stale".

gameName.description: The Riot ID as the caller spelled it, so a response can be matched back.

known.description: False when no account carries this Riot ID on this platform.

status.description:
`Active` or `Invalid` — the latter meaning account-v1 already 404'd on the
stored puuid and we recorded it. Null when bool AccountFreshnessReadModel.Known is false.

lastMatchIngestAtUtc.description:
When match ingestion last ran for this account. Null both when the account is unknown
and when it is tracked but its claim has never come up — the caller separates those
with bool AccountFreshnessReadModel.Known. That second case is the one worth acting on: the account is
in the population and has still never been fetched.

AccountFreshnessReadModel.description:
One Riot ID's intake state, for callers deciding whether an account is worth seeding.

     Deliberately tiny next to AccountExplorerReadModel. That one traces a Riot ID
through the whole pipeline — identity, lease, candidate funnel, mains, rank history — which
is what an operator inspecting one player wants, and far too much to ask thousands of times
in a row. A bulk caller only needs three facts: do we have it, is it still usable, and when
did we last ingest it.

AccountFreshnessRequestEntry.description: One Riot ID in an AccountFreshnessRequest.

AccountPipelineState.description:
The verdict ladder, resolved in declaration order — the first matching state
wins. Serialized as its name.

ActivityMode.description: Which window an activity series covers.

champions.description:
Champions whose newest aggregate row is oldest first, capped by
`DataQualityDetectors:FreshnessChampionLimit`.

championCount.description: Distinct champions with at least one aggregate row in the covered patches.

staleChampionCount.description: Champions whose newest row is older than the amber cadence.

staleAfterHours.description: The amber cadence, in hours, this breakdown judged against.

AggregateFreshnessReadModel.description:
The on-demand per-champion aggregate-freshness breakdown
(`GET /ops/data-quality/aggregate-freshness`). Split off the detector payload
because it is the one measurement that needs a grouped scan of
`champion_aggregate_scopes` — affordable on an explicit click, not on every page
view.

pendingSynergyMatches.description:
Queue-scoped matches not yet folded into the synergy aggregates (#922).
It has no timeline prerequisite, and it
starts at the full retained match count: the fold flag ships false for every
pre-existing row on purpose, so this reads as a large backlog on the first
deploy and drains over the following runs.

pendingEloBracketParticipants.description:
Tracked participants still missing their elo bracket stamp — rows the
rank-scoped aggregations cannot bucket yet. Served by the partial index
`IX_match_participants_elo_bracket_pending` (#2303). It does not drain to
zero on its own: rows of accounts without a rank snapshot stay pending until
the account's first snapshot arrives.

AggregationBacklogReadModel.description:
Work waiting on the aggregation side of the pipeline. Every counter reads
zero when aggregations are caught up with ingestion.

processName.description: The recorded ingestor process producing this family.

totalRowEstimate.description: Sum of the tables' planner estimates — approximate, like each of them.

distinctChampions.description:
Distinct champions the family holds rows for, exact (an index skip scan). For mains,
the champions with at least one active main.

oneOf.description: Latest recorded run of the producing process; null when it never ran.

AggregationFamilyReadModel.description:
One aggregation family (builds patterns, matchups, synergies, mains):
the tables it owns with their planner row estimates, its champion coverage,
and the latest run of the process producing it.

AggregationRunReadModel.description:
Rollup of the producing process's `process_runs` rows: the latest run's
outcome plus the last time it succeeded (they differ when the latest run
failed). JsonElement? AggregationRunReadModel.LastSuccessSummary is the JSONB payload the process
returned on its last success (e.g. per-run row/champion counts).

queueId.description: Queue the pipeline aggregates (soloq); backlog counts are scoped to it.

measuredAtUtc.description: When this payload was measured — it is served from a short cache.

AggregationsReadModel.description:
Health and coverage snapshot of every aggregation pipeline for the admin
     Aggregation panel: per-family row estimates, champion coverage, the latest
     recorded run, and the ingestion backlogs that should sit at zero when the
     pipeline is caught up.

     Every figure is a catalog lookup or an index probe (#2303): exact counts,
DISTINCTs and max()s over the fold tables were full scans that
took the page past a minute on a cold cache.

rowEstimate.description:
The planner's live-row estimate (`pg_stat_user_tables.n_live_tup`, the figure
`/database` prints), falling back to `pg_class.reltuples` when the statistics
view has no count yet.

ApexCutoffReadModel.description:
One day's apex thresholds. A tier is `null` when its league was not read that day
(a failed call, or the tier out of the ladder sync's scope).

ApexCutoffsReadModel.description:
Payload behind `GET /ladder/{platformId}/apex-cutoffs` (#2174): the region's
Grandmaster and Challenger thresholds, one entry per measured UTC day, oldest first.

AuditActionReadModel.description: An action name and the words the admin shows for it.

AuditEventReadModel.description: One operator action: who, what (string AuditEventReadModel.Label in plain words), on what, and its context.

actions.description: Every action name a writer records, with its plain words.

targetTypes.description: The kinds of entity an event targets.

AuditEventsReadModel.description:
One page of the operator-action trail for the admin Audit page and the known-player History
(#2288), newest first. The catalogs ride on every page so the filters need no extra call.

BuildCoreReadModel.description:
Dominant single choice per dimension within a build slice — the "core"
view at the top of a tab. Each entry mirrors the equivalent top-1
alternative in BuildVariationsReadModel; the duplication is
deliberate so the frontend can render the prominent header and the full
list independently.

pickRate.description:
Pick rate relative to the parent node — for a root child, this is
`games / firstItem games`; for a deeper child, it is
`games / parent.games`. Sums to ≤ 1 across siblings.

BuildVariationsReadModel.description:
Top-N variations per dimension within the slice, including the dominant
(which also appears in BuildCoreReadModel). Rune pages are
exposed at the build level via IReadOnlyList<BuildRunePageReadModel> ChampionBuildReadModel.RunePages,
not here.

ingestedMatchCount.description:
Number of `MatchParticipant` rows recorded for this candidate's PUUID,
i.e. how many of the account's games have already been ingested. Zero before
the Ingestor has processed the account.

oneOf.description:
The manual seed request that brought this candidate's account into the
pipeline, matched on `ResolvedPuuid` + `PlatformId`; null when the
candidate was surfaced organically by ladder discovery (no manual request).

CandidateDetailReadModel.description:
Full detail for one main-candidate: the candidate's own pipeline fields plus
the joined account identity, the count of match-participant rows already
ingested for the account's PUUID, and the linked `SeedRequest` when the
candidate's account was brought in by a manual "add a main" request (matched on
`ResolvedPuuid` + `PlatformId`). All three of the linked pieces are
optional: an organically-discovered, not-yet-ingested candidate carries none.

intakeLadder.description: Candidates inserted by ladder discovery (`Discovery`, summed over platforms).

intakeHarvest.description: Candidates inserted by the orphan-participant harvest (`Harvest`).

intakeManual.description: Candidates queued by an operator's manual seed (`ManualSeed`). Queued, not inserted: a manual seed promotes rows that discovery may already have created, so it is intake into the queue rather than into the table.

scored.description: Candidates scored by `Scoring`, summed over platforms.

promoted.description:
Candidates `Scoring` queued for ingestion — the per-platform top-N. The gap
against Scored is the competitive cut, not a failure.

validated.description:
Accounts whose candidates cleared ingestion (`MatchIngestion`). Null — not zero —
for periods before the counter existed; see
DateTime? CandidateFunnelReadModel.ValidatedFirstMeasuredAtUtc.

demoted.description:
Accounts `MainAnalysis` demoted back out of Validated on a critical play rate.
This is the funnel's only negative outcome: a candidate is in the pipeline, demoted back
into the pool, or pruned — there is no rejection verdict (#1029).

runs.description:
Runs of any of the six contributing processes that started in this period. Zero
separates "the pipeline did not run" from "it ran and moved nothing" — the whole point
of the panel.

CandidateFunnelBucket.description:
One period of the funnel. Intake is split by the process that produced it because the
three sources fail independently: ladder discovery drying up and the orphan harvest
drying up are different incidents with the same total.

buckets.description:
The series, oldest bucket first, contiguous from the oldest run on record to the
current period. Quiet periods inside that range are real zeros: runs happened,
they just moved no candidate.

windowDays.description: The window the caller asked for, in days, after clamping.

retentionDays.description:
How long `process_runs` keeps a run. A int CandidateFunnelReadModel.WindowDays larger than
this cannot be answered — the panel states the bound rather than drawing the
missing tail as zero throughput.

earliestRunAtUtc.description:
Start of the oldest run in the window, i.e. the earliest period this series can
speak for. Null when no run survives in the window at all — an empty range, not a
range of zeros.

validatedFirstMeasuredAtUtc.description:
Start of the first run whose summary carried the validated counter, which the
ingestor only began recording with #1024. Buckets entirely before it have a null
long? CandidateFunnelBucket.Validated: the pipeline was validating
accounts then, nothing was counting them, and a health panel may not pass off what
it did not measure as a measured zero (#924). Null when no run measured it yet.

CandidateFunnelReadModel.description:
Candidate-pipeline throughput over time (#1024): how many candidates entered, were
promoted, cleared ingestion and were demoted per period — as opposed to the
instantaneous status counts the rest of `/candidates` shows. A funnel can be
full and completely stalled, and the two look identical on a status list.

samples.description: Candidate rows that carried both ends of the leg.

p90Seconds.description:
The slow tail. Reported alongside the median because the two diverging is the shape a
backed-up queue has, and a median alone hides it.

CandidateLatencyLeg.description:
One leg of the queue, as a median and a p90 in seconds. Both are null when
Samples is 0: no row carried both timestamps, which is not a
latency of zero.

discoveredToScored.description:
Discovery to scoring, over candidates that have been scored. Measured from
`DiscoveredAtUtc` to `ScoredAtUtc`.

scoredToValidated.description:
Scoring to clearing ingestion, over candidates that have been validated. Measured
from `ScoredAtUtc` to `ValidatedAtUtc`.

retainedCandidates.description:
Candidate rows currently retained — the population every leg above is drawn from,
so a reader can see how much of it each leg actually covers.

CandidateQueueLatencyReadModel.description:
How long candidates currently in `main_candidates` took to move through the
queue (#1024): discovery → scoring, then scoring → validated.

gameName.description: Joined from `RiotAccount` on PUUID; null when not yet resolved.

tagLine.description: Joined from `RiotAccount` on PUUID; null when not yet resolved.

CandidateRowReadModel.description:
A single `MainCandidate` as surfaced to the list. MainCandidateStatus CandidateRowReadModel.Status is
the `MainCandidateStatus` name ("New"/"Scored"/"Queued"/"Processing"/
"Validated"). The Riot ID fields (string? CandidateRowReadModel.GameName,
string? CandidateRowReadModel.TagLine) are populated from the joined `RiotAccount` when one
exists for the candidate's PUUID; null when the account hasn't been resolved
yet (a candidate is discovered from mastery before its account is upserted).

totalCapped.description:
True when more rows match than the count reads: long CandidatesReadModel.Total is then
a lower bound ("10,000+"), not the exact figure.

CandidatesReadModel.description:
A page of main-candidate rows for the admin Candidates panel. Rows are
newest/most-relevant first. long CandidatesReadModel.Total is the count of the rows
matching the active filters (before paging) so the panel can render a pager,
counted up to a cap (#2304): past it, long CandidatesReadModel.Total is the cap and
bool CandidatesReadModel.TotalCapped is true.

CandidateStockAccounts.description:
The same reading as its CandidateStockBucket, counted in distinct
accounts — `(PlatformId, Puuid)` — instead of rows (#1534). Null on the bucket
when its reading predates the accounts figure: unmeasured, never 0. The statuses are
not disjoint in this unit — an account with one champion Validated and another Queued
counts in both — so they must not be added up into a total.

CandidateStockBucket.description:
One period's level, summed across platforms.

     Sampled, never summed across time. A period holding several hourly readings
reports its last one: a stock is a level, and adding two readings of the
same 419,000 queued candidates would report 838,000 of them. Across platforms within
that one reading the counts are summed — those are disjoint populations at a
single instant.

     Every status is present on every bucket, including the ones that read 0. A recorded
zero is a measurement — New at 0 means scoring drained its backlog, which is
the healthy state — and the read side must be able to tell it from an unmeasured
period, which is absent from IReadOnlyList<CandidateStockBucket> CandidateStockReadModel.Buckets entirely.

     Two units (#1534). The status counts are candidate rows — one per
(account, champion) — so they move whenever the number of rows per account does, not
only when throughput does. CandidateStockAccounts? CandidateStockBucket.Accounts carries the same reading in distinct
accounts.

buckets.description: One point per period, oldest first, empty before the first snapshot.

retentionDays.description:
The snapshot collection's TTL in days, so the panel can say why a 90-day window
came back holding less than 90 days of curve.

earliestSnapshotAtUtc.description:
The oldest snapshot in the window, or null when there is none. The series
genuinely begins here rather than at the window's left edge.

latestSnapshotAtUtc.description:
Wall-clock time of the most recent reading, for the panel's "as of" line. Null
when the step has never run.

CandidateStockReadModel.description: The candidate funnel's level over time (#1403): how many rows sat in each `MainCandidateStatus` at the end of each period, from the hourly snapshots the ingestor records. The companion of CandidateFunnelReadModel, which measures the same funnel's flow. Neither can be derived from the other: a period that scored 5,000 candidates and promoted 5,000 out of the pool leaves the level flat, and a flat level is exactly what a stalled pipeline also produces. Flow says how much moved, stock says how much is waiting. Forward-only, and never backfilled. The series starts at the first recorded snapshot (DateTime? CandidateStockReadModel.EarliestSnapshotAtUtc) and nothing before it is filled with zeros — the level then was not zero, it was unmeasured (#924). Reconstructing it afterwards is impossible in principle, not merely unimplemented: main_candidates has no QueuedAtUtc, so Scored and Queued cannot be told apart in the past, and pruning and demotion delete rows, so every past level would be understated by whatever has since been removed.

buildTree.description:
Item tree rooted at int ChampionBuildReadModel.FirstItemId. The root itself is
implicit (the tab already identifies it) — this is the list of its
direct children, each recursively carrying its own children.

runePages.description:
Top rune pages within this slice. All entries share the tab's
int ChampionBuildReadModel.PrimaryKeystoneId; variations live on the perks,
secondary tree, and stats.

ChampionBuildReadModel.description:
One tab on the champion page. Categorised by the combination of first
completed build item and primary keystone — both are required to be
non-zero. The tab body groups the slice's data into four sections:
BuildCoreReadModel ChampionBuildReadModel.Core, BuildVariationsReadModel ChampionBuildReadModel.Variations, IReadOnlyList<BuildTreeNodeReadModel> ChampionBuildReadModel.BuildTree,
and IReadOnlyList<BuildRunePageReadModel> ChampionBuildReadModel.RunePages.

oneOf.description:
Riot identity of this side; `null` for the aggregate of
the champion's mains, which has no single owner.

players.description:
Distinct accounts contributing to the column — always 1 for a single
player, the size of the main pool for the aggregate.

winRate.description: `wins / games`; 0 when the side has no games.

kda.description:
`(kills + assists) / deaths`, falling back to `(kills + assists) / games`
on a deathless sample so it stays on the same per-game scale as the metrics beside
it — the same convention the truemains leaderboard uses.

csPerMin.description:
Minions + neutral monsters per minute of game time, computed over the
summed durations so long games weigh proportionally.

goldPerMin.description: Gold earned per minute of game time, same denominator as double ChampionComparisonSideReadModel.CsPerMin.

sampleMet.description: Whether int ChampionComparisonSideReadModel.Games reached int ChampionMainsComparisonResponse.MinGames.

ChampionComparisonSideReadModel.description:
One column of the comparison. Counting stats are per-game averages so a
single player and a pool of mains stay on the same scale.

ChampionComparisonStatus.description: Why a comparison did — or did not — produce two comparable columns.

share.description: Share of the champion's archetype-classified games at this position and patch.

ChampionDamageBuildReadModel.description: The damage split of the games where the champion's build leaned on one archetype.

position.description: The lane this entry answers for, or null for the champion-wide entry a lookup falls back to.

profilePosition.description:
The lane the numbers were measured at: string? ChampionDamageProfileReadModel.Position itself, the champion's
best-covered lane on a champion-wide entry, null on a static fallback.

source.description: `measured` (folded from games) or `fallback` (a static classification, no shares).

patch.description: The patch the profile was folded on — may be older than the response's, by design of the snapshot.

physicalShare.description: Physical share of the damage to champions; with magic and true it sums to 1. Null on a fallback.

damagePerGame.description: Mean damage to champions per game — the weight a team bar gives this champion.

damageClass.description: `physical`, `magic` or `mixed` on a fallback; null on a measured entry, whose shares say more.

builds.description: The build archetypes above the games floor, most played first.

flexDamage.description: Whether two builds with opposite dominant damage types each hold a meaningful share of the games.

ChampionDamageProfileReadModel.description: One champion's damage profile, at one position or champion-wide.

patch.description:
The patch the snapshot was resolved for: the one asked for, or the newest patch carrying
profiles when none was. Null when nothing has been profiled yet.

profiles.description:
Per-position entries, then one champion-wide entry (`position: null`) per champion
for a pick at a position it has no entry for — the same resolution the item-context
fold applies — and the static fallbacks.

ChampionDamageProfilesResponse.description:
How every profiled champion splits its damage to champions by type (#1905) — one payload,
identical for every caller, so the desktop draft builds its team bars locally instead of
asking once per pick.

total.description: Lines the filters keep, across every page.

patchVersion.description: The resolved patch; empty when no aggregate data exists yet.

ChampionDirectoryPageReadModel.description:
One page of the champion directory (`GET /champions/directory`, #1734): the
`(champion, position)` lines the filters keep, in the requested order, with the
filtered total for the pager. Same envelope as `LeaderboardResponse`, plus the
patch the directory was resolved to — carried even on an empty page, so a page that
lists nothing still tells the patch picker which patch it is showing.

championId.description: Riot champion id (the admin resolves names from static data).

patch.description: Normalised "MAJOR.MINOR" patch.

lastAggregatedAtUtc.description: Newest `AggregatedAtUtc` across the champion's scope rows on that patch.

scopeRows.description: Scope rows behind the reading, so a one-account champion reads as thin rather than broken.

ChampionFreshnessRowReadModel.description: One champion's aggregate freshness on a patch.

axis.description: The situation, e.g. `EnemyMagicDamage`. The client owns the wording.

bucket.description: `High` or `Low` — the end of the axis where the item is picked more.

draftTime.description:
Whether a draft alone determines this situation. False for the gold-lead axis, which
a reader can only act on once the game is under way — the card has to say which kind
of advice it is giving.

rateOut.description: Pick rate at the opposite end.

lift.description: double ChampionItemContextAxisReadModel.RateIn minus double ChampionItemContextAxisReadModel.RateOut, always positive.

patchWindow.description: Patches folded into this finding — 1 when the served patch was deep enough alone.

ChampionItemContextAxisReadModel.description: One situation that moves an item's pick rate.

slot.description: The decision this verdict is about.

parentItemId.description: The item this step followed, 0 on the branch every build starts from (and on every boots and starter verdict, which are decided before any item exists). A client looks a verdict up by slot and parent and item: the same item after a different parent is a different decision.

games.description: Games of the slice that took this branch to this item.

branchGames.description: Games of the branch the pick rate is over: those that reached the parent and completed a further item.

winRate.description: Win rate of the games that built it. Null when the sample is empty.

patchWindow.description:
Widest patch window behind the findings below: 1 when the served patch carried them
on its own. The card prints it, because "over the last three patches" is a different
claim from "this patch".

axes.description: Qualifying situations, strongest first. Empty for `Core` and `Preference`.

ChampionItemContextItemReadModel.description: One step's verdict — one edge of the build tree (#1496).

patch.description: The patch the verdicts describe, resolved when the caller sent none.

allRanks.description: Always true today — see the remarks. Present so the client never has to assume it.

routes.description:
The build path of every build item and boots above (#2183): its components in the order
the mains buy them. Served for the site to show later; the desktop app reads the same
order on the next-item answer.

ChampionItemContextResponse.description:
The situational build context of one champion slice (#1450, read surface #1451): for
each step the slice's builds actually take, whether the item is core, situational or a
preference, and — when situational — the draft situations that measurably move it.

games.description: Games behind the order: the mains' games that bought at least one component before completing it.

ChampionItemRouteReadModel.description: An item and the order its components are bought in — the champion page's form of the build path.

patch.description:
Resolved patch (`major.minor`) both sides were computed for, or
`null` when the caller pinned none and the slice spans
every patch still held by retention.

position.description:
Riot team position both sides were narrowed to, or `null`
when the comparison spans every lane.

minGames.description:
Games each side needs before the comparison is considered meaningful
(`ChampionsList:MinComparisonGames`). Exposed so the caller can say
how far a thin sample is from the bar instead of just hiding the panel.

status.description: Outcome of the lookup — see ChampionComparisonStatus.

oneOf.description:
The compared account's side. Null only when the Riot ID is unknown to us
(ChampionComparisonStatus.UnknownAccount) — a known account
with no games on the champion still yields a side with zero games.

The yardstick column: by default the aggregate of every tracked main of this champion, excluding the compared account itself. A `main` target narrows it to that one account's games on the champion. The target is resolved as any account we hold — it is deliberately not required to be flagged a main of this champion, so a caller can measure themselves against a specific rival. Only the default (pool) column is restricted to actual mains. The UI only ever offers real mains as targets. Targeting the compared account itself is allowed and answered honestly: both columns describe the same games, so they are identical and every delta is zero. That is the arithmetic being right, not a special case — it earns no guard and no status of its own. The picker drops the compared account from its options so the UI never leads anyone into it. Null when the account is unknown, or when a targeted account is.

ChampionMainsComparisonResponse.description:
Head-to-head read model returned by
`GET /champions/{championId}/mains-comparison` (issue #528): one Riot
account's numbers on a champion set against the champion's mains — either
the whole main pool (ProfileIdentityReadModel? ChampionComparisonSideReadModel.Identity
null) or a single named main.

Both sides are computed from the same population, queue, patch and lane
scope, so the two columns are directly comparable. Build / skill order and
early-game leads are deliberately out of scope here (a separate issue
covers them).

The endpoint never reaches out to Riot: the account must already exist in
our database, and an unknown Riot ID resolves to
ChampionComparisonStatus.UnknownAccount rather than an error.

winRate.description:
int ChampionMatchupEntry.Wins / int ChampionMatchupEntry.Games. int ChampionMatchupEntry.Games is always
at least the minimum-games floor here, so this never divides by zero.

playRate.description:
Share this opponent holds of the champion's total matchup games in the same
scope — int ChampionMatchupEntry.Games over the games summed across every opponent, before
any floor. The quantity the leaderboard's floor is expressed in
(double ChampionsListOptions.MinMatchupPlayRate), returned
so a client can say "you meet this opponent in 4% of your games" rather than
leaving a bare game count to mean whatever the reader assumes. The
single-opponent search reads one row, so it takes its denominator from a second
aggregate over the same scope rather than from the row itself.

Zero only on the player-scoped route, whose live join is narrowed to the one
opponent and holds no such total.

winRateLowerBound.description: Lower bound of the 95% Wilson interval around double ChampionMatchupEntry.WinRate — "at worst, this matchup is this good". This is what the best-matchups list is ranked by, not double ChampionMatchupEntry.WinRate: ranking the raw rate makes the leaderboard a small-sample detector, because on a wide enough field the most extreme rate is always the thinnest sample. A 62% over 96 games bounds at 53%, a 53% over 995 games bounds at 50%, and a 82% over 11 games bounds at 52% — which is the whole point, since eleven games cannot establish an 82% matchup.

winRateUpperBound.description:
Upper bound of the same interval — "at best, this matchup is only this good" —
and the key the *worst*-matchups list is ranked by, ascending. Deliberately not
the mirror of the lower bound: a bad matchup is one whose ceiling is low, and
using the lower bound at both ends would rank the worst list by which sample is
thinnest, reintroducing at the bottom exactly what the top was fixed for.

laneWinRate.description:
Share of *decided* lanes the champion won against this opponent — ahead by
     more than the configured gold threshold at 15 minutes (#919).

     The denominator is int ChampionMatchupEntry.DecidedLaneGames, not int ChampionMatchupEntry.Games: a
match with no ingested timeline, or one that ended before 15 minutes, cannot
be judged, and a lane inside the threshold band was neither won nor lost.
Dividing by games played would understate every figure here.

     `null` when nothing can be said: fewer decided lanes than
int ChampionsListOptions.MinDecidedLaneGames (which
includes none at all). Every global slice carries it, search included — both
halves of that row come from the same aggregate rows, so the lane sample can no
longer exceed the games it sits beside. A player-scoped slice judges its
lanes live from the player's own 15-minute snapshots (never the population-wide
aggregate) and has no floor: one decided lane is a rate, like one game is a row.
Never a substitute zero.

decidedLaneGames.description:
Lanes actually decided — won or lost past the threshold — and so the sample
double? ChampionMatchupEntry.LaneWinRate rests on. Always smaller than int ChampionMatchupEntry.Games,
often much smaller early on, which is why it is returned rather than left for
the client to guess.

averageGoldDiffAt15.description:
Mean gold gap over the lane opponent at 15 minutes, in gold, signed from the
     champion's point of view (#976). This is the *magnitude*
     double? ChampionMatchupEntry.LaneWinRate cannot carry: a lane won 60% of the time by 120 gold
     and one won 60% of the time by 1200 are the same rate and a different matchup.

     Averaged over int ChampionMatchupEntry.GoldDiffLaneGames — the lanes the gap was actually
summed over, which for rows folded before #976 is fewer than
int ChampionMatchupEntry.DecidedLaneGames and often zero. `null` then,
never 0: "we have not measured this gap" and "the lane is dead even" are the
opposite of interchangeable here, since 0 is the most decisive-looking value
the number can take.

goldDiffLaneGames.description:
Lanes double? ChampionMatchupEntry.AverageGoldDiffAt15 is averaged over. Returned so the client
can withhold a verdict on a sample too small to band, rather than turning three
lanes into a confident label.

averageXpDiffAt15.description:
Mean experience gap over the lane opponent at 15 minutes, signed from the
     champion's point of view (#1111) — the second half of "who is ahead", and not
     a restatement of double? ChampionMatchupEntry.AverageGoldDiffAt15. Gold is who bought more,
     XP is who is bigger; a lane won on kills while losing waves shows a gold lead
     over an XP deficit, which is a lead the next all-in reverses.

     `null` when the gap was never measured over this scope, never
0 — same rule as the gold gap, and for the same reason: 0 is the most
decisive-looking value the number can take.

xpDiffLaneGames.description:
Lanes double? ChampionMatchupEntry.AverageXpDiffAt15 is averaged over. Its own counter rather
than a reuse of int ChampionMatchupEntry.GoldDiffLaneGames: rows folded before #1111 carry
gold and no XP, and borrowing the gold denominator would report those as a
dead-even lane out of data that does not exist.

ChampionMatchupEntry.description:
A single lane opponent's head-to-head line: how the champion fared against
this opponent across the scoped games.

patch.description:
Resolved patch the slice was computed for (`major.minor`), or
`null` when the caller did not pin a patch and the
slice spans every patch with data.

matchups.description:
One entry per lane opponent above the minimum-games floor, ordered by
double ChampionMatchupEntry.WinRate descending.

ChampionMatchupsResponse.description:
Lane-matchups read model returned by the champion matchup endpoints. Lists
how a champion performed at a position against every lane opponent (same
`TeamPosition`, opposite `TeamId`) it met over the scoped games.

Served from the pre-aggregated `champion_matchup_stats` (#606) for every
global slice — leaderboard and single-opponent search alike. Only the
player-scoped route is computed live from `match_participants`, because
the aggregate carries no account dimension. (The rows are stored floor-free,
so the search reading them keeps its "answer from one game up" contract; the
earlier claim that an aggregate "built at floor 10" could not serve it was
never true of the storage, only of the read.)
