The leaderboard drops opponents below the larger of
int ChampionsListOptions.MinMatchupGames and
double ChampionsListOptions.MinMatchupPlayRate × the
champion's total matchup games in the same scope; the search applies neither.

IReadOnlyList<ChampionMatchupEntry> ChampionMatchupsResponse.Matchups is ordered by double ChampionMatchupEntry.WinRate
descending, but the best / worst slicing is *not* that order — see
double ChampionMatchupEntry.WinRateLowerBound.

patch.description: The patch the model was served for, resolved when the caller sent none; null when the champion has no model at this position.

oneOf.description: The next legendary item, or null when the build has no open branch left.
The boots, or null when the game already holds a pair the mains settle on.

order.description:
The build as one row (#2101): what is completed, the next step — the boots when they
are due — then the likely rest, the boots at the step the mains complete them at.
Empty when the champion has no model at this position.

situation.description: Where the game sits on every situation the model could evaluate, axis name to bucket.

enemyLanes.description: The enemy lanes the situation was computed against, the caller's own first, then the solver's.

ChampionNextItemResponse.description:
What to complete next in one live game (#1749): for each open slot, the items the
champion's mains continue into from where this game stands, ranked by the share the
model predicts for a game in this one's situation.

patchVersion.description:
Canonical `major.minor` patch IReadOnlyList<ChampionOverviewRowReadModel> ChampionOverviewReadModel.TopRows was computed for —
the patch the site serves. Not necessarily the newest patch with data: a patch
too thin to fill a directory is skipped (#1109). Says nothing about
long ChampionOverviewReadModel.GamesAnalyzed, which spans the whole aggregate history.

gamesAnalyzed.description:
Every game the aggregate table holds for the tracked queue, all patches
summed — the site's lifetime volume, not this patch's. Deliberately not
patch-scoped: a figure the homepage prints without a qualifier must not fall
every time a patch rolls over, and "how much has TrueMain measured" is the
question the chip actually answers. Counts below-floor and position-less
scopes too, like long ChampionSummariesResult.TotalGames does per
patch; not the sum of IReadOnlyList<ChampionOverviewRowReadModel> ChampionOverviewReadModel.TopRows (a short slice).

topRows.description:
The strongest rows on the patch, tier-then-score ordered (S first,
strongest within a tier first), truncated to the requested limit.

ChampionOverviewReadModel.description:
Homepage-sized snapshot of the champion directory (`GET /champions/overview`,
#972): the all-time "games analyzed" total plus a short, pre-sorted slice of the
strongest rows, so the homepage never has to fetch and sort the full ~500-row
directory just to render a stat chip and an 8-row teaser. The teaser is scoped to
the active patch, no elo bracket filter — the homepage has none of its own.

tier.description: OPGG-style performance tier — see string ChampionSummaryReadModel.Tier.

banRate.description: Share of observed matches that banned this champion; null before #920's ban data. See double? ChampionSummaryReadModel.BanRate.

ChampionOverviewRowReadModel.description: One row of IReadOnlyList<ChampionOverviewRowReadModel> ChampionOverviewReadModel.TopRows — the homepage teaser's shape, not the full directory row.

eloBracket.description:
Elo filter this slice was computed for — `ALL`, a bare tier
(e.g. `GOLD` — that tier only) or a `TIER_PLUS` form
(e.g. `GOLD_PLUS` — that tier and above), per
`Core.Lol.Ranking.EloBracket`. The builds, skill orders and win
rates below are scoped to it. `ALL` by default.

eloCoverage.description:
Games in the selected bracket as a fraction of all games on this
champion at the resolved patch + position (across every bracket). Lets
the page show how representative a high-bracket slice is. Always
`1.0` for the `ALL` bracket.

minSampleMet.description:
False when int ChampionResponse.TotalGames is below the minimum-sample floor
for a trustworthy build (tiny high-bracket slices). The page still
renders the data but flags it as low-confidence.

totalGames.description:
Total games across the scope, including patterns that are excluded
from IReadOnlyList<ChampionBuildReadModel> ChampionResponse.Builds (no first item, pick-rate below the floor,
or beyond the top-N cap). Used as the denominator for
double ChampionBuildReadModel.PickRate.

totalWins.description:
Total wins across the same scope as int ChampionResponse.TotalGames. Frontend
derives the champion-wide win rate from `TotalWins / TotalGames`.

ChampionResponse.description:
Top-level read model returned by `GET /champions/{id}`. Lists the
dominant ChampionBuildReadModel tabs for a champion at a
given patch + position, each tab keyed by (first completed item, primary
keystone).

ChampionScalingResponse.description:
How a champion's win rate changes with game length, at a position. Win rate
is bucketed by game duration; double? ChampionScalingResponse.ScalingIndex is the win-rate gap
between the longest and shortest qualifying bucket (positive = scales into
the late game). Read from the `champion_scaling_stats` aggregate (#1368).

ChampionStatRow.description:
Per-champion corpus row for the admin champions panel. long ChampionStatRow.Games is
the raw participation count over `match_participants` (honouring the
region/patch/position/queue filters); the main/otp/extended-sample counts come
from `main_champion_stats` and are scoped by region only — patch, position
and queue do not apply to that table (it is computed per account-champion, not
per match). Champion names are intentionally omitted: the frontend resolves them
via DDragon.

pickRate.description:
Share of TrueMain games on this position taken by this champion —
a main-population pickrate, derived from the same
`champion_aggregate_scopes` rows as int ChampionSummaryReadModel.Games /
int ChampionSummaryReadModel.Wins / double ChampionSummaryReadModel.LanePlayRate. Not a meta-wide
ratio: the denominator is the sum of scoped games for this position
on the patch, not every observed game on the patch.

lanePlayRate.description:
Share of this champion's own games played on this position — i.e. the
champion's role distribution. A champion played 60% mid / 40% top has
`LanePlayRate = 0.6` on its mid row and `0.4` on its top row.

banRate.description:
Share of the observed matches on this patch that banned the champion (#920).
     Lane-independent — a ban happens before roles exist — so every row of a
     champion carries the same value.

     `null` means "not observed", not "never banned": bans are
read from champion_ban_stats, which only has rows for matches ingested
since the feature shipped, and Riot payloads are not retained so older patches
could not be backfilled. Clients must render the gap rather than a 0%.

     Its denominator is every observed match, unlike double ChampionSummaryReadModel.PickRate, whose
denominator is tracked mains' games at this lane. The two are therefore not
addable — which is why no pick+ban "presence" figure is offered.

tier.description: OPGG-style performance tier (`S` / `A` / `B` / `C` / `D`) for this `(champion, position)` on the active patch. Computed by ChampionTierCalculator from a pick-rate + ban-rate + win-rate blend (#971 — presence-first, weighted toward pick and ban rate over a sample-shrunk win rate), then bucketed by percentile within this row's own position — not against the whole patch mixing every lane — so a thin lane can't out-rank a much larger, genuinely competitive one just for having few peers to beat. Defaults to string string.Empty until assigned.

tierScore.description:
The blended score (#971) that placed this row in string ChampionSummaryReadModel.Tier,
scoped to this row's own position (see string ChampionSummaryReadModel.Tier). Matches the
score `GET /champions/tierlist` computes for the same
`(champion, position)` row given the same `(patch, eloBracket)`
— both endpoints tier one lane at a time. Useful for ordering this
endpoint's own rows (e.g. the homepage teaser) by tier strength without
re-deriving an ad-hoc sort.

oneOf.description:
Most-played build for this `(champion, position)` on the active
patch — keystone, secondary tree, item sequence. Null when no
pattern rows exist (rare; e.g. positions with summary games but no
observed builds yet).

ChampionSummaryReadModel.description:
One row of the champion directory (`GET /champions`) — one entry per
`(champion, position)` pair, computed against a single patch (the
requested one, or the global latest if unspecified). A champion played in
multiple lanes therefore surfaces once per lane.

position.description: Lane the champion is played in for this slice.

patch.description:
Resolved patch (`major.minor`), or `null` when the
slice spans every patch with data.

partnerPosition.description:
The partner lane the caller narrowed to, or `null` when
every lane is included.

minGames.description:
Minimum games a pair needed to appear in IReadOnlyList<ChampionSynergyEntry> ChampionSynergiesResponse.Partners. Echoed so
the caller can explain an empty list instead of implying "no synergy".

championGames.description:
Games behind double ChampionSynergiesResponse.ChampionWinRate — the tracked-player sample this
champion's own baseline rests on. Zero means the champion has no recorded
games in the scope, so IReadOnlyList<ChampionSynergyEntry> ChampionSynergiesResponse.Partners is necessarily empty.

championWinRate.description:
The champion's own win rate at this lane over the scoped games. One of the
two inputs to every entry's expected win rate.

cohortWinRate.description:
Win rate of the whole tracked cohort in the scope — the reference point ally
win rates are measured against. Published rather than hidden because it is
what makes the expected values reproducible: a partner sitting exactly here
contributes nothing to the expectation.

partners.description:
One entry per qualifying teammate, ordered by
double ChampionSynergyEntry.Synergy descending (best partner first).

ChampionSynergiesResponse.description:
Champion synergies read model (#922) — "you play this champion at this lane,
who should your friends play?". Lists the teammates a tracked player on this
champion actually won more (or less) with than their individual win rates
predicted, read from the pre-aggregated `champion_synergy_stats` table.

The ranking value is double ChampionSynergyEntry.Synergy, not
double ChampionSynergyEntry.WinRate: a raw pair win rate mostly restates
how strong the two champions are on their own, which is what the tier list is
for. Every entry carries its own int ChampionSynergyEntry.Games so a
caller can show what a number is built on, and only pairs above the
int ChampionSynergiesResponse.MinGames floor are returned at all.

partnerPosition.description: Lane the partner played — always different from the champion's.

games.description: Games the two were on the same team, at these two lanes.

winRate.description:
int ChampionSynergyEntry.Wins / int ChampionSynergyEntry.Games. int ChampionSynergyEntry.Games is always at
least the response's `minGames` floor, so this never divides by zero.

playRate.description:
Share of the champion's own games this partner was on the team for — the
quantity double ChampionsListOptions.MinSynergyPlayRate
floors, returned so a caller can say "you have this teammate in 3% of your
games" instead of leaving a bare count to mean whatever the reader assumes.

partnerBaselineGames.description:
Games behind double ChampionSynergyEntry.PartnerBaselineWinRate — always at least
int ChampionSynergyEntry.Games, since it counts every game this champion was a tracked
player's teammate, not only the ones alongside the queried champion.

partnerBaselineWinRate.description:
The partner's marginal win rate: how often a tracked player's team won with
this champion at this lane on it, across all its partners. This is
deliberately not the partner's own solo win rate as a tracked main — that
population is a specialist on their champion, while a partner is whoever
showed up, and mixing the two biases every expectation upward.

expectedWinRate.description:
What the pair should have won given the two marginals and the cohort
reference point, combined in log-odds space (`Core.Lol.Synergy.SynergyMath`).

synergy.description:
double ChampionSynergyEntry.WinRate − double ChampionSynergyEntry.ExpectedWinRate. Positive means the
pairing added something beyond the two champions being individually good.

pickRate.description:
Share of TrueMain games on this position taken by this champion — the
same main-population pickrate as double ChampionSummaryReadModel.PickRate.

banRate.description:
Share of observed matches that banned this champion, or `null`
when the patch predates ban ingestion — see
double? ChampionSummaryReadModel.BanRate, which this is copied from.
Feeds the tier score (#971, second-highest weight after pick rate) whenever
this field's patch has ban data at all; on a patch with none, the ban term
is dropped from the blend and its weight folds into pick rate and win rate
so tiers stay comparable across ban-data and no-ban-data patches — see
ChampionTierCalculator.

ChampionTierEntryReadModel.description:
A single `(champion, position)` row of the tier list. Mirrors the
directory's metrics so the page can render winrate / pickrate and link
straight to the champion page.

entries.description:
Rows in this tier, ordered strongest-first by the same blended score
that placed them in the bucket (see
ChampionTierCalculator).

ChampionTierGroupReadModel.description: One S/A/B/C/D bucket and the champion rows that fell into it.

patchVersion.description: Canonical `major.minor` patch the tiers were computed for.

position.description:
The position the list is scoped to (`TOP` / `JUNGLE` /
`MIDDLE` / `BOTTOM` / `UTILITY`), or `null` when the
caller asked for every position at once. When null, tiering is still
computed independently within each position.

tiers.description:
Tier groups in descending strength (S first), each carrying its ranked
champion rows. Empty tiers are omitted, so a sparse patch may surface
fewer than five groups.

ChampionTierListReadModel.description: The champion meta / tier-list view (`GET /champions/tierlist`) for a single patch, optionally narrowed to one position. Champions are grouped into S / A / B / C / D tiers by a pickRate + banRate + winRate blend (#971 — presence-first: pick and ban rate outweigh a sample-shrunk win rate), with the tiering computed per position — an S-tier mid laner is S among mid laners, not against the whole patch — so the page reads as a meta ranking for the role the user is filtering on. Every metric is derived from the same champion_aggregate_scopes rows the champion directory reads (see ChampionSummaryReadModel); nothing here is synthesised. The tier thresholds are documented on ChampionTierCalculator.

pickRate.description:
Share of TrueMain games on this position taken by this champion on the
patch — the same main-population pickrate definition used by
double ChampionSummaryReadModel.PickRate.

banRate.description:
Share of the patch's observed matches that banned this champion, across all
elo bands unless the request carries a rank filter. `null`
on any patch older than ban ingestion (#920) — see
double? ChampionSummaryReadModel.BanRate. Early on, most of the series
is null, so consumers must handle a partly-null series rather than assume the
column is present on every point.

ChampionTrendPoint.description:
A single patch's aggregated rates for the champion trend series. Every
rate is a fraction in `[0, 1]`, derived from the light per-patch record
(`champion_patch_stats` + the ban pair, #1957) — the scopes the directory
and detail endpoints read, summed per patch, and still there once a patch's
full aggregates are purged; never synthesised. int ChampionTrendPoint.Games is surfaced
so the frontend can flag thin patches.

position.description:
Position every point is computed for. Empty string when the champion
has no positioned rows in the record (the series is then empty too).

points.description:
One entry per patch that has data for this `(champion, position)`,
ordered oldest → newest so the chart's X axis reads left-to-right in
release order.

ChampionTrendReadModel.description:
Winrate / pickrate evolution for a single champion across recent patches
(`GET /champions/{id}/trend`). Powers the trend chart on the champion
detail page so users can see whether a champion is climbing or sliding.
The series is pinned to one position — the requested one, or the
champion's dominant lane on the latest patch when unspecified — so every
point in IReadOnlyList<ChampionTrendPoint> ChampionTrendReadModel.Points is comparable.

patch.description:
Resolved patch (`major.minor`), or `null` for every
patch still inside the retention window.

minGames.description:
Minimum games a trio needed to appear in IReadOnlyList<ChampionTrioSynergyEntry> ChampionTrioSynergiesResponse.Completions. Echoed
so a caller can say "no third pick has been played with this duo often
enough yet" rather than "this duo has no good third".

pairGames.description:
Games the duo itself played together in the live window. This is the ceiling
every completion's sample is drawn from: a duo with 30 games can never offer
a third pick with more than 30.

pairWinRate.description:
int ChampionTrioSynergiesResponse.PairWins / int ChampionTrioSynergiesResponse.PairGames, or 0 when the duo has no
recorded games in the window.

completions.description:
One entry per third pick above the floor, ordered by
double ChampionTrioSynergyEntry.Synergy descending. Empty whenever the
duo is too rare to support a third dimension — the expected case, not an error.

ChampionTrioSynergiesResponse.description:
Trio completions for an already-chosen duo (#922): "you play this champion,
your friend plays that one — what should the third pick?".

Unlike the duo slice this is NOT pre-aggregated. The pair space is bounded by
(champion × lane × partner × lane), but the triple space multiplies that by a
third champion and lane, which is both far larger and almost entirely empty —
most triples are never played, and the few that are carry single-digit samples.
Storing it would cost orders of magnitude more rows than it could ever answer,
so a trio is computed on demand from `match_participants`, narrowed first
to the games where the chosen pair actually played together. That keeps the
query bounded by the pair's own game count rather than by the champion's.

The consequence is a scope difference worth surfacing: the pair figures here are
counted over the currently-retained matches, while the duo endpoint reads an
aggregate that also holds frozen older patches. The two therefore describe the
same pairing over different windows and their game counts will not match — which
is why int ChampionTrioSynergiesResponse.PairGames is returned explicitly instead of being taken
from the duo response.

games.description: Games the full trio played together.

baselineGames.description:
Games behind the third pick's marginal win rate — read from the same
baseline table the duo slice uses, so a trio and a duo judge a champion
against the same reference.

expectedWinRate.description:
What the trio should have won given all three marginals: the queried
champion's own rate plus both allies', combined in log-odds space against
the cohort reference point.

ChampionTrioSynergyEntry.description: A single third pick's line for the chosen duo.

patch.description: Normalised patch filter applied, null when unfiltered.

pageSize.description: Page size the server actually used (after clamping).

total.description: Selected games across all pages — the recommendation's sample.

truncatedGames.description:
Selected games past match retention (#2368): they count in the recommendation but keep
nothing to list, so they are outside int CompositionBuildGamesResponse.Total and the pages.

maxPossibleScore.description:
Score a game reproducing every requested slot would reach; the
denominator of each game's int CompositionGameReadModel.Score.
Zero when the draft carried no composition slot — every game then
scores 0 and the ratio is undefined rather than 0%.

games.description:
The page's games, in the selection's own order: games piloted by a main
of the champion first, then best similarity, recency breaking ties.

CompositionBuildGamesResponse.description:
Response of `POST /champions/{id}/composition-build/games`: the games
the recommendation was actually computed from, in selection order, one page
at a time (#940). Separate from the recommendation payload on purpose — the
matchup page refetches the build on every draft edit, and hydrating a
hundred match rows on each keystroke for a panel most visits never open
would be paid by everyone.

gamesConsidered.description: Games the aggregation ran over (the top-K size).

oneOf.description: Single-element item set, mirroring the champion-page shape.

Most supported opening of the completed-items build order (up to the
first three legendaries, in completion order).

firstItemId.description:
First completed item of BuildItemPathReadModel? CompositionBuildRecommendation.CorePath (the build-tree root),
0 when no core path was resolved.

buildTree.description:
Pruned item-progression tree of the sampled games that opened with
int CompositionBuildRecommendation.FirstItemId — same shape the champion page renders.

CompositionBuildRecommendation.description:
Build recommendation aggregated from the top-K most similar games of the
composition recommender (#563), win-weighted. Reuses the champion-page
build vocabulary (BuildRunePageReadModel and friends) so the
frontend renders both from the same components. Every dimension is
nullable: a sparse top-K (missing timeline data, no rune selections) drops
the dimension instead of fabricating one.

position.description: Position the player queues for. Required.

patch.description: Optional patch filter (major.minor or full game version).

eloBracket.description: Optional elo filter (band or `_PLUS` cumulative form).

allies.description:
Known allied picks, excluding the player's own champion (a slot at the
player's position is rejected — that slot is the route's champion).
Nullable so an explicit `"allies": null` reads as an empty draft
instead of tripping MVC's implicit-required validation.

enemies.description: Known enemy picks. Null reads as empty, like IReadOnlyList<CompositionSlotInput>? CompositionBuildRequest.Allies.

player.description:
Optional Riot ID (`Name#TAG` or the `Name-TAG` slug): only that player's
games are sampled — a truemain's own build against this draft (#1987). Unknown → 404.

CompositionBuildRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /champions/{id}/composition-build`. POST
because the input — up to nine champion/position slots across both teams —
is too rich for query parameters. Both slot lists are optional and may be
partial: the composition is a ranking signal, never a hard filter.

patch.description: Normalised patch filter applied, null when unfiltered.

eloBracket.description: Resolved elo filter token (`ALL` when unfiltered).

matchupRequested.description:
True when the draft pinned the role opponent — the matchup is then a
hard requirement on the sampled games, not a ranking signal.

matchupFound.description:
False only when the role opponent was requested and no recorded game
has that matchup — the build is then empty and the client should fall
back to the champion's baseline build.

lane.description:
How the lane went in the sampled games (#1117) — measured over exactly the games
CompositionConfidenceReadModel CompositionBuildResponse.Confidence counts, so the tool's stat line describes one population
throughout. It used to read the matchup aggregate instead, whose champion side is
mains-only (#1087), which showed "—" beside a sample of eight games whenever no
main had played the matchup.

CompositionBuildResponse.description:
Response of `POST /champions/{id}/composition-build`: the win-weighted
build recommendation for the requested draft plus the confidence signals
the frontend surfaces — how much data backs it and how close the sample
actually got to the requested composition. Sparse data must read as
sparse, never as fabricated certainty.

sampleSize.description: Games actually aggregated (the selected top-K size).

candidatePoolSize.description: Candidate games scanned (bounded by the configured pool cap).

truemainGameCount.description:
How many of the aggregated games were piloted by a main of the champion
(mains are preferred in selection).

maxPossibleScore.description: Score a game reproducing every requested slot would reach.

meanSimilarity.description: Mean of score/max over the selected games, in [0, 1].

CompositionConfidenceReadModel.description:
Confidence signals of one recommendation: the sample that was aggregated,
the pool it was drawn from, and how similar the sample is to the requested
draft (0 when no composition slot was provided — the recommendation then
degrades to the champion's most recent games at the position).

profileIconId.description: Riot profile icon id, 0 when never resolved.

CompositionGamePilotReadModel.description: Riot identity of a sampled game's pilot.

score.description: Similarity score of the game, out of `MaxPossibleScore`.

isTruemain.description: True when the pilot is an active main of the champion.

oneOf.description:
The pilot's Riot identity, null when the game's participant carries no
resolved Riot account (harvested rows can pre-date account resolution).

match.description: The pilot's slice of the game, in the match-feed row shape.

CompositionGameReadModel.description:
One sampled game: the collapsed match row, its similarity score, and who
piloted it — the two things the aggregation weighed it on.

measuredGames.description:
Sampled games where both lane sides had a 15-minute reading. Smaller than the
sample: a game that ended before the mark, or whose timeline was never ingested,
is a game but not a judgeable lane.

decidedGames.description:
Of int CompositionLaneReadModel.MeasuredGames, those settled past the gold threshold either
way. Lanes inside the band are decided by neither side and belong to neither —
which is why this is stored rather than derived from the measured count.

winRate.description:
Share of int CompositionLaneReadModel.DecidedGames the champion was ahead in.
`null` when none were decided — never 0, which would read as
"the lane is always lost".

averageGoldDiffAt15.description:
Mean gold gap over the lane opponent at 15 minutes, across
int CompositionLaneReadModel.MeasuredGames — evens included, since an even lane is exactly what
the counters above cannot express. `null` when nothing was
measured.

averageXpDiffAt15.description:
Mean experience gap over the same games. Beside the gold rather than derived
from it: gold is who bought more, XP is who is bigger, and a lane won on kills
while losing waves shows one ahead and the other behind.

CompositionLaneReadModel.description:
The lane at 15 minutes over a recommendation's own sample. Three denominators
because they are three different questions: how many of the sampled games could be
judged at all, how many of those were actually decided, and — for the gaps — the
judged ones again, evens included.

CompositionSlotInput.description: One known pick of the draft: a champion at a position.

sources.description: Every `CrashSource` name, for the source filter.

processes.description: The producing processes ("Api", "Ingestor"), for the process filter.

CrashesReadModel.description:
A page of recorded process crashes for the admin Crashes panel. Entries are
newest-first. long CrashesReadModel.Total is the count of all rows matching the active
filters (before paging). IReadOnlyList<string> CrashesReadModel.Sources and IReadOnlyList<string> CrashesReadModel.Processes ride on
every response (static catalogs) so the panel can populate its filter selects
without a Mongo `distinct`.

CrashExceptionReadModel.description: One link in a crash's exception chain.

CrashLogTailReadModel.description: One buffered log line attached to a crash report.

id.description: The crash document's identifier — a 24-char hex string (the Mongo ObjectId).

explanation.description:
Plain-language reading of the crash (#722), derived from the source, the
exception chain and — for unclean shutdowns — the memory snapshot and exit
code. Heuristic display text; the raw fields below remain authoritative.

recentLogTail.description: The last log lines (Information+) before the crash, oldest-first.

CrashReportReadModel.description:
A single recorded crash. string CrashReportReadModel.Source is the trigger ("HostRun",
"AppDomainUnhandled", "TaskSchedulerUnobserved", "UncleanShutdown"). For an
unclean shutdown the exception fields are null and the memory fields carry the
dead run's last-known snapshot (the OOM signal).

status.description:
`green` | `amber` | `red` | `unknown`. Unknown means the
detector could not compute its answer — it is never used for "measured and fine".

count.description:
The card's headline number, or null when unknown. What it counts is stated by
string DataQualityDetectorReadModel.CountLabel and differs per detector (duplicate groups, stale
aggregations, orphan rows in the sample…).

countLabel.description: What long? DataQualityDetectorReadModel.Count counts, as a noun phrase.

headline.description: One sentence answering "so what": the verdict in words, with the numbers in it.

unknownReason.description:
Why the answer is unknown. Set if and only if DetectorStatus DataQualityDetectorReadModel.Status is
`unknown`, so the panel can always explain the state instead of showing a
blank card.

sourceNote.description:
The detector's data source and cost, for the operator reading the panel: which
tables it looks at and why that is affordable on a page view.

rows.description: The drill-down: one row per audited table / platform / family / patch.

thresholds.description:
The configured levels this detector judged against, echoed so the panel states the
line it drew rather than leaving the operator to guess it from a colour.

hasDrillDownEndpoint.description:
True when a heavier, on-demand endpoint can expand this detector (currently only
the per-champion freshness breakdown), so the panel knows whether to offer it.

label.description: Table, platform, process, patch or check name.

value.description: The row's primary number, or null when it could not be measured.

valueLabel.description:
The row's number as the panel should print it (with its unit), or null when
unmeasured. Formatted here so a percentage, a count and an age can share one row
type without the front end branching on the detector.

oneOf.description:
The verdict of the measure string? DataQualityDetectorRowReadModel.ValueLabel prints, when it is not the
     row's own (#1656).

     A row can judge more than one measure — the orphan card judges a share and its
movement — and DetectorStatus DataQualityDetectorRowReadModel.Status is the worst of them. Painting the printed
number with that verdict puts a warning colour on a reading that is fine and hides
which measure actually tripped. Null means the printed number is the
judged one and carries DetectorStatus DataQualityDetectorRowReadModel.Status.

note.description: Why this row reads the way it does, or what it is measuring.

DataQualityDetectorRowReadModel.description:
One drill-down row. Deliberately generic: a label, its own verdict, a number and a
pre-formatted qualifier, which covers "a dimension table with N duplicate groups",
"a platform whose newest match is 3 h old" and "a patch with 412 matches" without a
per-detector payload shape.

detectors.description: One entry per detector, in a stable presentation order.

evaluatedAtUtc.description:
When the detectors ran. Every age on the panel is relative to this, so a stale
browser tab cannot silently age its own numbers.

DataQualityDetectorsReadModel.description:
The automated anomaly detectors behind the admin data-quality panel (#924): one card
     per detector, each carrying its own verdict, headline number and drill-down rows.

     The shape is deliberately uniform — a detector is a status, a number and a list of
rows — so the panel renders any number of detectors with one component, and adding
the next detector is a backend-only change. The prose lives here rather than in the
front end because a threshold and the sentence explaining it have to move together;
this is an operator-only, English-only surface (no i18n), so there is nothing to be
gained by splitting them across two repositories' worth of files.

issueType.description: The DataQualityIssueType name (camelCase on the wire).

count.description: Total matches flagged by this check across the active filters.

matches.description: Newest-first sample of flagged matches (bounded by the page size).

DataQualityIssueGroupReadModel.description: One issue type's flagged matches: a capped sample plus the full count.

DataQualityIssueType.description:
The data-quality checks the panel can run, each independently listable. The
camelCase name is what crosses the API boundary and what the `issue` query filter accepts.

label.description: What the levels apply to (e.g. "duplicate groups").

amber.description: Amber level, or null when disabled.

red.description: Red level, or null when disabled.

unit.description: Unit of the two levels: `count`, `percent`, `hours` or `ratio`.

direction.description:
Which side of the level is the bad one: `above` (a count, an age or a share
that has to stay low) or `below` (a floor — a patch whose match volume has to
stay near the median). The panel cannot infer this from the number, and without it
a printed level is ambiguous: "warning at 40%" reads as a ceiling when it is a
floor.

DataQualityThresholdReadModel.description: One configured green/amber/red boundary, echoed for display.

databaseBytes.description:
What actually occupies the volume that day: measured `pg_database_size`
(catalogs included) plus Mongo's own on-disk size, summed because both engines
share one volume (#1023). This, not long DbStorageDailyPoint.TotalBytes, is what the
forecast projects.

postgresBytes.description:
The Postgres half of long DbStorageDailyPoint.DatabaseBytes, so the panel can show the
split instead of asserting one opaque total. 0 when the day has no Postgres
reading.

mongoBytes.description:
The Mongo half of long DbStorageDailyPoint.DatabaseBytes. 0 for every day before #1023
shipped and in environments where Mongo is unconfigured — which is why the
forecast only fits days measuring the same engines as the latest one.

totalBytes.description:
Sum of the per-object sizes: `pg_total_relation_size` over
`public`-schema tables, plus each Mongo collection's storage + indexes.

rowEstimate.description: Sum of the planner's live-tuple estimates. A trend figure, not an audit count.

DbStorageDailyPoint.description: One day's totals across the whole database.

bytesPerDay.description: Least-squares slope of database size against time, in bytes per day.

diskCapacityBytes.description: The configured volume size the thresholds are percentages of.

DbStorageForecast.description: The fitted growth rate and when it reaches each configured fill level.

daily.description: Days covered, oldest first. Empty until the snapshot step has run.

tables.description:
The largest tables, each with its own series. Capped by
`StorageHistory:TopTables`; smaller tables still count towards
long DbStorageDailyPoint.TotalBytes, they just are not charted.

engines.description:
The storage engines the window actually contains readings for — `postgres`,
`mongo`, or both (#1023). The panel states it rather than implying the
figures are the whole disk: before the first Mongo snapshot lands, and in any
environment where Mongo is unconfigured, the totals cover Postgres only.

comparableDays.description:
How many of the most recent days the forecast is actually allowed to fit: the
     trailing run of days measuring the same engines as the latest one. Equal to
     IReadOnlyList<DbStorageDailyPoint> DbStorageHistoryReadModel.Daily's length in the steady state, and smaller only just after
     an engine started or stopped being measured — the day Mongo first appears adds
     its footprint in one step, and a step is not a growth rate (#1023).

     Exposed rather than left implicit so the panel can name the real reason a
forecast is missing instead of re-deriving the rule with its own heuristic and
drifting from this one.

oneOf.description:
Null when no projection can honestly be made: fewer than three days of
history, flat or shrinking storage, or no configured disk capacity. Never a
placeholder — the panel shows why instead.

DbStorageHistoryReadModel.description:
Storage growth over a window, plus the disk-exhaustion forecast (#925). Read
entirely from the daily snapshot collection — the page never runs a
`pg_catalog` scan of its own, which is the point of snapshotting.

DbStorageTablePoint.description: One table's size on one day.

engine.description: Which engine owns the object: `postgres` or `mongo`.

bytesPerDay.description:
Average bytes added per day across the window (first to last observation,
divided by the days between them). Negative when the table shrank.

rowsPerDay.description: Average rows added per day, on the same first-to-last basis.

growthRate.description:
Growth over the window as a fraction of the starting size (0.25 = +25%). Null
when the table started the window at zero bytes — the growth is then undefined
rather than infinite, and the absolute figures already say what happened.

DbStorageTableSeries.description: One table's growth over the window.

percent.description: Fill level as a percentage of the disk (80, 90, 100…).

projectedAtUtc.description:
Projected crossing date. Null when it lands more than a century away in either
direction — no meaningful date at this rate, rather than a spurious one. A date
in the past means the level is already breached.

DbStorageThresholdCrossing.description: When the fitted line reaches one fill level.

DedicationPart.description: A part of the Truemain score.

points.description: Score points this part contributed (unrounded; the parts sum to the score).

maxPoints.description: Score points this part can contribute at most — its weight × 100.

DedicationPartReadModel.description: One part of the score and what it contributed.

score.description: Final score, 0..100 (one decimal). The sum of IReadOnlyList<DedicationPartReadModel> DedicationReadModel.Parts' points.

championId.description: The champion the score is about: the player's most-played main (their signature champion), or the filtered one.

isOtp.description:
The verdict: true when the player is a one-trick on int DedicationReadModel.ChampionId.
The same `main_champion_stats.IsOtp` flag the OTP badge and the
`otpOnly` filter read, so the three can never disagree.

playRate.description: Raw share of the player's recent ranked games spent on the champion (0..1).

championGames.description: Recent ranked games on the champion — the numerator of double DedicationReadModel.PlayRate.

recentGames.description: Recent ranked games the play rate is measured over — its denominator.

masteryPoints.description: Riot champion-mastery points on the champion. Null until the mastery has been read.

masteryRank.description: 1-based rank of the champion in the player's mastery by points. Null until read, or when Riot has no entry for it.

daysSinceLastPlayed.description: Whole days since the player last played the champion, per Riot mastery. Null until read.

parts.description: Each part's contribution, in the order the UI lists them (heaviest first).

DedicationReadModel.description: TrueMain's signature metric for a player's signature champion — shown as the Truemain score; the wire name stays `dedication` so existing links (`?sort=dedication`) keep working (#1701). Ships the raw facts and each part's contribution in score points, so the UI explains the number with figures that add up instead of asserting it — the formula lives in DedicationScore and is documented in `docs/dedication-score.md`.

role.description: Which container of the process (the ingestor's job mode); null for the Api.

previousVersion.description: The version it replaced; null on the process's first recorded boot.

deployedAtUtc.description: When the process booted on string DeploymentReadModel.Version: the rollout time.

DeploymentReadModel.description: One process booting a new version.

deployments.description: Every version change in the window, oldest first.

DeploymentsReadModel.description:
The version changes of every backend process over a window (#2297), drawn by the admin
time-series charts as deploy markers. A restart on the same version is not in it.

version.description: The release's version, without the tag's `desktop-v` prefix; checked by the service.

DesktopDownloadRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /internal/desktop/downloads` (#1805): one installer the site's
download route just redirected a visitor to.

label.description: What the admin page calls it, from the catalog.

DesktopKeyUsage.description: One page or feature: how often it was used in the window, and by how many installs.

DesktopShare.description: A count of installs behind one value — a version, an operating system.

installId.description: The install's anonymous id, drawn by the app on its first launch.

appVersion.description: The app's version, e.g. `0.3.1` or `0.3.2-beta.4`; checked by the service.

firstLaunch.description: True in the batches of the launch that drew Guid? DesktopTelemetryRequest.InstallId.

openMinutes.description: A batch covers at most a day of the app being open.

pageViews.description: Page key → views. Keys outside the catalog are dropped, not rejected.

features.description: Feature key → uses. Keys outside the catalog are dropped, not rejected.

DesktopTelemetryRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /desktop/telemetry` (#1805): what one install of the desktop app
counted since its previous batch. Counters, not events — the app adds them up between two
sends, and the API adds the batch to the install's day.

windowDays.description: The requested window in days, after clamping; today included.

usageRetentionDays.description: The usage collection's TTL in days: no window reaches further back than this.

earliestDayUtc.description: The first day with a recorded download or usage in the window, or null when there is none.

active.description: Distinct installs seen today, over the last 7 days and the last 30, whatever the window.

days.description: One bucket per day from DateTime? DesktopUsageReadModel.EarliestDayUtc to today, oldest first.

versions.description: Installs active in the window, by the version of their latest day, most installs first.

operatingSystems.description: Installs active in the window, by operating system, most installs first.

downloadVersions.description: Downloads in the window by version, newest first by first download day.

pages.description: Every page the app counts, used or not, most viewed first.

features.description: Every feature the app counts, used or not, most used first.

DesktopUsageReadModel.description:
The admin portal's view of the desktop app (#1805): installers downloaded from the site and
     what the installed apps did, over a chosen window of UTC days ending today.

     Measured from the first day anything was recorded, never before. The series starts at
DateTime? DesktopUsageReadModel.EarliestDayUtc: the app did not report anything before the version that sends
telemetry, and those days were unmeasured, not empty.

installs.description: Distinct installs that reported at least once in the window.

newInstalls.description: Installs whose first launch fell in the window.

activeInstallDays.description: Install-days in the window: the denominator of the time open per active day.

DetectorStatus.description:
A detector verdict. Ordered by declaration only; precedence lives in
    `DataQualityDetectorEvaluator.Worst`.

score.description:
The ranking key: how far behind our pick (or pool) is into this champion,
shrunk by its games, times how often it is played on our lane. Zero for a
suggestion from the ban-rate fallback. Not a win probability and not meant
to be displayed.

reasons.description:
The facts behind the suggestion, strongest first: `laneThreat` (our
pick is behind into it) or `banRate` (the fallback: how often it is
banned) — see DraftReasonKind.

DraftBanCandidateReadModel.description: A champion worth banning, and why (#1906).

plannedPick.description: The pick the player declared (their own hover), if any.

pool.description: The player's pool with its mastery points, protected when no pick is declared.

allyChampions.description: Allies' champions, locked or hovered — never suggested.

DraftBanRequest.description: The champion-select state the ban suggestions need, as posted by the client.

targetChampionIds.description: The champions protected: the declared pick, or the pool members weighed.

DraftBanResponse.description: The ban suggestions for one champion-select state.

delta.description: Expected matchup delta over the available opponents we have games on, weighted by play rate on the lane.

losingInto.description: Of int DraftBlindReadModel.LikelyOpponents, how many the pick is clearly behind into.

likelyOpponents.description: How many of the lane's most-played available opponents int DraftBlindReadModel.LosingInto counts over.

DraftBlindReadModel.description: Blind-pick safety: the expected matchup over the lane opponents still available.

matchupDelta.description:
Win rate against the enemy in our lane minus this champion's win rate at
the lane overall, both from `champion_matchup_stats`. When the lane
guess is split between several enemies, each one's delta weighted by the
chance the solver gives it of being our opponent (#1906).

matchupGames.description: Games the matchup rests on. Zero means no enemy in our lane, or the pairing is unseen.

blind.description:
The expected matchup before the lane opponent is known: the deltas into
the opponents still available, weighted by how often each is played on the
lane, with how many of the most-played ones the pick is clearly behind
into (#1906).

strengthDelta.description:
The champion's win rate at the lane minus the lane's average win rate —
how strong the pick is on its own, before any matchup.

strengthGames.description: Games the strength rests on: the champion's games at the lane.

enemyDelta.description:
Observed-minus-expected win rate against the enemies on the board beyond our
lane (#1713), each weighted by the chance it plays elsewhere than our lane.

enemyGames.description: Games the enemy-team figure rests on, across every measured enemy.

synergyDelta.description:
Mean observed-minus-expected win rate with the allies on the board (locked,
and hovered at half weight), straight from the site's synergy figures —
a mean since #1906, so four allies do not outweigh one lane.

synergyGames.description: Games the synergy rests on, across every measured ally.

teamFitDelta.description:
Team composition (#1906): the mean, over the axes the board can place our team on
(allies' magic share, frontline count), of the candidate's win rate in that band
minus its win rate overall. Zero until three allies are on the board. Weighed 0 in
double DraftCandidateReadModel.Score until the back-test sets it.

teamFitGames.description: Games the team-composition figure rests on: the largest band's.

score.description:
The ranking key: the lane term (the opponent where the board shows one,
the blind expectation for the rest), the champion's strength at the lane,
the enemy team, the team composition, then the ally term, each delta shrunk
towards zero by its games. Deliberately not called a win probability, and
not meant to be displayed.

thinSample.description:
True when the lane reading in play and the synergy both rest on fewer
games than their floor. A display flag: the shrinkage already orders thin
candidates.

reasons.description:
The two or three facts that carry the pick, strongest first, as data: the
client writes the sentence, the numbers stay the endpoint's.

patch.description:
The patch the matchup figures were read from — the current one, or
`current+previous` when the current patch was too thin for this champion.

DraftCandidateReadModel.description:
A pick we could make, and why it ranks where it does.

The components stay separate all the way to the client on purpose: the
panel has to be able to say a pick is good *because the lane is favourable*,
*because it is safe blind* or *because it fits the team*, which a single total
cannot express. Every figure is a measured win-rate difference in probability
points with the games behind it; none is a win probability.

position.description: Riot team position the guesser placed it in.

confidence.description:
0..1. Half means a coin flip between two readings, not "half right" —
the panel must render it as a guess, because the matchup, runes and build
underneath all rest on it.

pinned.description: True when the user corrected this slot by hand.

DraftEnemyLaneReadModel.description: One enemy champion placed in a lane, and how sure we are.

DraftReasonKind.description: What kind of fact a DraftReasonReadModel states.

delta.description: A win-rate difference in probability points (0.031 = +3.1 pts).

rate.description: A plain rate (0..1) — a lane-phase win rate, a ban rate.

probability.description: The solver's probability that an enemy is our lane opponent — a lane guess, not a chance to win.

share.description: Share of the lane's games a champion is played in.

axis.description: The composition axis a `teamFit` reason reads.

bucket.description: The band of string? DraftReasonReadModel.Axis the board puts our team in.

tentative.description: True when the fact rests on an ally's hover rather than a lock.

DraftReasonReadModel.description:
One measured fact behind a suggestion. Text-free on purpose: the fields a
kind uses are listed on DraftReasonKind, the others are null.

patch.description: The current patch the answer reads.

previousPatch.description:
The patch added when the current one is too thin for a champion (#1906);
each candidate's `patch` says whether it was.

enemyLanes.description: The enemy side as the guesser placed it.

laneOpponentChampionId.description:
The enemy the guesser put in our lane, or null while no enemy has been
placed there yet. Null is a normal early-draft state, not an error.

laneOpponentConfidence.description:
How sure we are about the lane opponent specifically — the one number
the whole panel hangs on.

laneOpponentProbability.description:
The solver's probability that our lane opponent is already on the board,
over every placement it weighs (#1906). Below 1, the blind figures carry the
rest of the lane term.

DraftRecommendationResponse.description: The whole answer to one champion-select state, in one payload.

enemyChampions.description: Enemy champions picked or hovered so far.

pinnedEnemyLanes.description: Lanes the user corrected by hand, by enemy champion id.

previousEnemyLanes.description:
The placement currently on screen, so an equally-good re-solve does
not reshuffle the panel between two picks.

allies.description: Allies already locked, keyed by lane.

hoveredAllies.description: Allies hovering a champion they have not locked, keyed by lane (#1906).

candidates.description: The player's champion pool, to rank.

DraftRequest.description: The champion-select state, as posted by the client.

processes.description: One entry per process, sorted by process name.

EffectiveConfigurationOverviewReadModel.description:
What every host is actually running with (#1034): one entry per process, each grouped
into the allow-listed sections EffectiveConfigurationCatalog
declares for it.

processName.description: Which host bound these values — `Api` or `Ingestor`.

version.description: The build this process is running, or null for a plain local build.

capturedAtUtc.description:
When this snapshot was taken. For the Api this is always "now" — it is built live
on every request. For the Ingestor it is the boot time of its last run: still what
that process is running, even if older than the last deploy.

sections.description: The allow-listed sections, in catalog order.

EffectiveConfigurationProcessReadModel.description: One process's snapshot: which build, which environment, and its sections.

description.description: One sentence saying what this section controls.

values.description: The rendered values, in the order the properties are declared on the options class.

EffectiveConfigurationSectionReadModel.description: One configuration section's worth of values, with the prose explaining what it drives.

value.description: The pasteable-back-into-configuration form. Null when the option is unset.

valueLabel.description: The humanised form ("90 days", "1.0 TB"), or null when it would repeat string? EffectiveConfigurationValueReadModel.Value.

source.description: Which provider supplied an override, e.g. `environment`. Null for `default`/`derived`.

unit.description: How to read the number — see EffectiveConfigurationUnits.

notice.description: Set when the value is unset and that has a visible consequence elsewhere in the portal.

EffectiveConfigurationValueReadModel.description: A single bound option, as the process holds it.

oneOf.description: The run's final summary (a JSON object); omit to keep the last heartbeat's.
The run's current summary (a JSON object); omit to only refresh the heartbeat.

ExternalProcessRunStartedResponse.description: Answer to `POST /ops/process-runs`: the id the script heartbeats and finishes with.

processName.description: One of the external process names the API accepts (`PersonaScraper`, `OtpSeeder`).

host.description: The machine the script runs on, shown next to the run.

jobMode.description: How the run was started (e.g. `weekly`, `manual`), optional.

oneOf.description: Initial summary (a JSON object), optional.

ExternalProcessRunStartRequest.description: Request body for `POST /ops/process-runs`: an ops script starts a run.

participantCount.description: Actual `match_participants` row count for this match.

expectedParticipantCount.description: Expected participant count for the queue, or null if the queue is unknown.

issues.description:
Every issue this match is flagged by (a match can trip several checks),
as DataQualityIssueType names.

FlaggedMatchReadModel.description: A single flagged match row in the list.

patches.description: The patches pooled, newest first; empty when nothing has been folded yet.

minSamples.description: The sample a tier needs before its quartiles are served.

tiers.description: Tiers in ladder order (Iron first); a tier with no sample at all is absent.

FormBenchmarkResponse.description:
The form benchmark of one position (#2076): for every tier with data, how many laners'
games were sampled and the quartiles of the figures the desktop dashboard's form tiles
show. Like the pace benchmark, every tier is answered and the app picks the player's own
locally, so the rank it reads from the League client never leaves the machine.

tier.description: The ranked tier, as the `EloBracket` ladder spells it (e.g. `DIAMOND`).

samples.description: Laners' games counted (one per participant on the lane).

oneOf.description: `(kills + assists) / deaths`, deaths floored at one, per game.
Share of the team's kills the player took part in, 0 to 1, per game.
Minions plus jungle monsters killed per minute of game.
Deaths per game.
Vision score per minute of game.

FormBenchmarkTierReadModel.description:
One tier of a position. Every quartile is null under
int FormBenchmarkResponse.MinSamples: the tile then shows no reference rather
than one drawn from a handful of games.

HealthAlertChangeKind.description: What a health alert announces about a key: it started failing, or it recovered.

enabled.description: False when no channel is configured: the alerter is off and IReadOnlyList<HealthAlertReadModel> HealthAlertsReadModel.Alerts only holds history.

channel.description: The channel alerts go to (`discord`), or null when off.

redConfirmations.description: Consecutive red evaluations before a signal counts as failing.

processFailureThreshold.description: Consecutive failed runs at which a process is announced.

lastEvaluatedAtUtc.description: When the alerter last evaluated; null when it never has (or Mongo is not configured).

openIncidents.description: Keys of the signals and processes with an incident open right now.

HealthAlertsReadModel.description:
The `/health` page's alerts panel (#2292): whether the alerter is on, the rules it
applies, and the last alerts it sent.

total.description: Distinct matches flagged by at least one active check.

staleTimelineThresholdHours.description:
Matches with `TimelineIngested = false` are only flagged once older
than this many hours, so the normal recovery backlog isn't reported as
stuck. Echoed back so the panel can label the threshold it's seeing.

IncompleteMatchesReadModel.description:
A page of flagged matches for the data-quality panel, grouped by issue type.
IReadOnlyList<DataQualityIssueGroupReadModel> IncompleteMatchesReadModel.Groups carries the (capped) sample of matches per issue plus
the full count, so the panel renders "N matches" headers without paging every
row. long IncompleteMatchesReadModel.Total is the distinct flagged-match count across the
active filters (a match flagged by several checks is counted once).

sum.description: Their sum: a counter's total, a histogram's summed value.

IngestorInstrumentReadModel.description: One instrument over the window, its series by total descending.

mean.description: double IngestorMeterSeriesReadModel.Sum / long IngestorMeterSeriesReadModel.Count: a histogram's mean measurement.

IngestorMeterSeriesReadModel.description: One tag set of an instrument over the window.

retentionDays.description: The rollup retention the API is configured with, in days; null when the TTL is disabled.

oldestRetainedUtc.description:
The oldest rollup still stored; null when none is, meaning nothing was ever recorded —
not a quiet window. Measuring started with #1636, so a window reaching further back
than this was only partly measured.

IngestorMetricsReadModel.description:
The Ingestor's own meter over a window, for the admin Riot API tab (#1636): every
instrument it recorded, each split by tag set. Summed from the per-minute rollups its
meter exporter writes; an instrument that recorded nothing in the window is absent.

patch.description: The game data's `major.minor` patch, or `latest`.

items.description: Every classed item, by id; an item can have several classes, its main one first.

ItemClassesResponse.description:
The in-game shop's class of every item that has one — what the desktop kit editor's item
picker filters by, as the shop does: Fighter, Marksman, Assassin, Mage, Tank, Support.

classes.description: The class names (`Fighter`, `Marksman`, …), the item's main class first.

ItemContextClass.description: What a verdict says about an item (#1450).

ItemContextSlot.description:
Which decision an item context row describes (#1450). The slots are read from
different resolvers and answer different questions, so a verdict never mixes them:
"which legendary do I complete", "which boots do I take", "what do I start with", and
"when do the boots come".

cost.description: The component's full shop price, before anything held is taken off it.

share.description: Share of the measured games that bought it at this rank; null when the order is the recipe's.

measured.description: True when the order comes from the mains' purchases, false when it is the recipe's.

components.description: The component's own components in the same terms, for an intermediate (Lost Chapter); empty for a basic item.

ItemRouteStepReadModel.description:
One component on the way to an item (#2183), at its place in the order the champion's
mains buy them — or, when too few games measured it, at its place in the recipe.

processes.description: The lane's processes by duty cycle descending.

LaneDutyCycleReadModel.description:
The share of wall-clock time a lane (the job mode a host ran as) had at least one
process running over the window, from the recorded process runs. `unassigned`
gathers runs recorded without a job mode.

secondary.description: Second lane when its share is meaningful (≥ the share floor and below the primary), otherwise null.

LeaderboardPositionsReadModel.description:
Primary / secondary lane for a leaderboard row, derived from the
position-share distribution across the player's mains. string LeaderboardPositionsReadModel.Primary
is the highest-share lane; string? LeaderboardPositionsReadModel.Secondary is the next lane whose
share clears the noise floor (and is below the primary), null otherwise.
Positions are Riot uppercase strings (TOP/JUNGLE/MIDDLE/BOTTOM/UTILITY).

score.description: The exact value used for ORDER BY in SQL — exposed so the UI can show the sort key alongside the raw tier/LP.

pageSize.description: Number of rows per page (the value the service clamped to).

total.description: Total rows across all pages for the active filter — drives the page-count UI.

LeaderboardResponse.description:
Paged response shape for `GET /truemains`. Mirrors
MatchSummariesResponse so the frontend's pagination controls
behave identically across leaderboard and match-history pages.

rank.description: 1-based position on the filtered leaderboard, computed server-side so the UI doesn't need to track `(page-1)*pageSize`.

region.description: One of `europe`, `americas`, `korea`. Rows from platforms outside those buckets never reach the leaderboard.

oneOf.description: Null when the account has no rank snapshot yet — those rows sort last via NULLS LAST.

topChampions.description: Up to 3 most-played champions, ordered by descending games. Empty when no main-champion analysis has run.

oneOf.description:
The player's primary and secondary lane, derived from position share across
their main champions (same share logic as the profile, #205). Null when no
main-champion analysis has run, so the UI omits the role icons entirely.

Dedication score (0..100) for the row's signature champion — the sort key
behind `?sort=dedication`, and the column shown on every row
whichever sort is active. Under a `championId` filter the score is
about that champion; otherwise it is about the player's top main. Null
when no main-champion analysis has run for the account.

The known player this account belongs to (#2016) — the row shows their name, linking to
`/players/{slug}`. Null for an account no source attributes to anyone.

LeaderboardRowReadModel.description:
One row of the truemains leaderboard (`GET /truemains`). Identity comes
from `riot_accounts`, ranked from the latest `rank_snapshots` per
account, stats from a participant aggregate on the same page slice, and top
champions from `main_champion_stats` filtered to `IsMain=true`.

games.description: Games on the player's tracked main champions, summed from `champion_aggregate_scopes`. May be 0 while int? LeaderboardStatsReadModel.Wins/int? LeaderboardStatsReadModel.Losses are non-zero — those are the overall ranked totals, this counts only tracked mains.

wins.description: Overall ranked-split wins from the latest `rank_snapshots` row (League-V4), independent of which champions are tracked. Null when the snapshot has no win/loss totals.

losses.description: Overall ranked-split losses from the latest `rank_snapshots` row. Null when the snapshot has no win/loss totals.

winRate.description: `wins / (wins + losses)` over the overall ranked split (from the latest rank snapshot) when both are known, otherwise null — the frontend hides the cell instead of rendering 0% / NaN.

kda.description:
`(kills + assists) / deaths` across attributed participant rows, falling back to
`(kills + assists) / games` on a deathless sample so the value stays on the same
per-game scale as the metrics beside it. Null when there are no attributed rows.

playRate.description: The player's authoritative play rate for this champion (0..1), as stored by main analysis (`games / total games on the account`).

isOtp.description:
True when the player is a one-trick pony on this champion — double LeaderboardTopChampionReadModel.PlayRate
clears the OTP threshold (`MainAnalysisOptions.OtpPlayRateThreshold`, 85%),
as flagged at ingest time by main analysis. Drives the "OTP" badge on the row.

primaryKeystoneId.description: Keystone rune of the player's dominant build for this champion. Null when no aggregated build exists for the player on this champion.

secondaryStyleId.description: Secondary rune tree of the player's dominant build for this champion. Null when no aggregated build exists.

firstItemId.description: First completed item of the player's dominant build for this champion. Null when no aggregated build exists.

id.description:
The log document's identifier. A 24-char hex string (the Mongo ObjectId)
since logs moved off Postgres (#416). The admin viewer already accepts a
string or numeric id, so the response shape is unchanged.

eventType.description:
The registered ops-event name (e.g. `CandidateValidated`) when this
row is a named domain event (#444); null for plain diagnostics.

traceId.description:
`HttpContext.TraceIdentifier` of the request the row was written during,
i.e. the `traceId` of the ProblemDetails the client received (#1555).
Null for rows written outside a request.

requestMethod.description: HTTP method of the request the row belongs to (#1555).

requestPath.description: Path of the request the row belongs to, with its query when the writer included it (#1555).

statusCode.description: Status code the request answered with, when known (#1555).

durationMs.description: Request duration in milliseconds, when measured (#1555).

LogEntryReadModel.description:
A single persisted log line. string LogEntryReadModel.Level is the
`Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.LogLevel` name (e.g. "Warning", "Error");
string? LogEntryReadModel.Exception is the formatted exception when one was logged (else
null); string? LogEntryReadModel.ProcessName identifies the producing host ("Api" /
"Ingestor") when stamped.

accepted.description:
Entries handed to the log channel. Lower than the batch only when the log store
is off in this environment; the channel's own overflow is reported as a
`LogRecordsDropped` row, not here.

LogIngestAcceptedResponse.description: Response of `POST /internal/logs`: how many entries were queued for persistence.

timestampUtc.description: When it was first seen, by the frontend's clock; replaced by the server's when implausible.

level.description: Warning and above only: the ops logs are signal, and so is what is forwarded to them.

requestPath.description: A route template (`/api/champions/{n}`), not a raw path: the forwarders aggregate on it.

count.description: How many identical occurrences this entry stands for since the previous report.

LogIngestEntry.description: One reported error, possibly standing for several identical occurrences (int? LogIngestEntry.Count).

process.description:
Only the two frontends may report, and the edge through the admin (#1580); `Api`
and `Ingestor` rows come from those hosts' own loggers and cannot be forged
through this endpoint.

LogIngestRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /internal/logs` (#1556): a batch of errors one frontend
process observed. Every bound is enforced before anything is written, because the
endpoint turns a request body into rows an operator reads.

eventTypes.description:
Every known ops-event name (the static `OpsEvents` catalog, #444), so
the admin Logs panel can populate its event filter without a Mongo
`distinct` per load. Independent of the active filters.

processes.description:
The producing processes ("Api", "Ingestor"), for the process filter —
static catalog, independent of the active filters.

LogsReadModel.description:
A page of persisted application/process logs for the admin Logs panel.
Entries are newest-first. long LogsReadModel.Total is the count of all rows
matching the active filters (before paging), so the panel can render a pager.

MainCandidateSource.description:
Where a MainCandidate came from. Ladder candidates are
mastery-gated ladder crawl results (rank/points populated); ManualSeed are
operator-added accounts; Harvest are derived from orphan
`match_participants` rows (observed games/wins, no mastery data). The
source selects how `ScoringProcess` scores the candidate.

queueKnown.description: True when the queue has a known profile (count/position rules apply).

hasLanes.description: True when `TeamPosition` is meaningful for this queue.

issues.description: Issue types this match is flagged by, as DataQualityIssueType names.

teams.description:
One entry per team. For lane queues each team is laid out across the five
canonical positions (missing slots flagged); for laneless queues the slots
are the raw participants in roster order.

MatchDataQualityDetailReadModel.description:
Per-match detail: both teams laid out by position with the gaps identified.
Returned by `GET /ops/data-quality/match/{id}`.

eventType.description: Riot event type: ITEM_PURCHASED / ITEM_SOLD / ITEM_DESTROYED / ITEM_UNDO.

beforeId.description: On an ITEM_UNDO, the item id that existed before the undo (Riot `beforeId`).

afterId.description: On an ITEM_UNDO, the item id that exists after the undo (Riot `afterId`).

MatchDetailLaning15ReadModel.description: Laning-phase diffs @15 (this participant minus their lane opponent).

gameName.description: Riot game name when the participant is a tracked account, else null.

tagLine.description: Riot tag line when the participant is a tracked account, else null.

teamPosition.description: Riot team position (TOP/JUNGLE/MIDDLE/BOTTOM/UTILITY); empty when unknown.

items.description: Inventory slots 0..5 (length 6) — the trinket is in int MatchDetailParticipantReadModel.TrinketItemId.

roleBoundItemId.description:
Riot's role-bound slot, outside the six inventory slots: a bot laner's boots once the
role quest is done, the other roles' quest reward. 0 when empty or not recorded.

keystoneId.description: The keystone perk id (slot 0 of the primary tree); 0 when the page failed to ingest.

cs.description: Sum of lane minions + neutral monsters.

oneOf.description: Approximate rank tier at game time (closest snapshot). Null when no snapshot exists.

killParticipation.description:
Kill participation — `(kills + assists) / teamKills`, 0 when the team
scored no kills. Usually 0..1 but can exceed 1 when a player's kills plus
assists outnumber the team's total kills (shared assists are double-counted).

performanceScore.description:
TrueMain performance score, 0–100 — a weighted, role-aware blend of KDA,
kill participation, damage share, gold share, CS/min, vision/min and the
@15 laning leads. See `Core.Lol.Performance.PerformanceScore` for the
full model and its weights.

placement.description:
1-based rank of this participant's int MatchDetailParticipantReadModel.PerformanceScore within the
match (1 = best of all 10). Ties break on takedowns, then deaths, then
participant id, so the placement is always a strict 1..N.

isMvp.description: True for the top-scoring participant of the winning side.

isAce.description: True for the top-scoring participant of the losing side.

oneOf.description: Laning diffs @15 vs the opposing `TeamPosition`. Null when either side lacks a @15 snapshot.

firstToLevelTwo.description:
True when this participant reached level 2 (their 2nd skill point)
strictly before their lane opponent. Null when there is no opponent in
the same `TeamPosition` or either skill timeline is missing.

runes.description: Full rune page (6 selections): the primary tree (keystone first) then the secondary tree.

itemEvents.description: Build order (purchases / sells / undos) in chronological order.

skillEvents.description: Skill order (Q/W/E/R level-ups) in chronological order.

MatchDetailParticipantReadModel.description:
One participant's full slice: identity, scoreboard line, build order, skill
order, rune page and the derived per-minute / laning stats.

MatchDetailReadModel.description:
Full single-match detail payload backing
`GET /truemains/{nameTag}/matches/{matchId}`. Everything the three
detail tabs (General scoreboard / Details build+lane / Runes) need in one
round trip: the match header, all 10 participants with their build order,
skill order, rune page and timeline-derived laning stats.

Per the story's "Out of scope" list this carries no team-objective counters
and no ward counts — only data already in the DB. Derived per-minute rates,
laning diffs and the performance score / placement / MVP / ACE accolades
(#639) are computed server-side so the frontend renders them directly.

selectionIndex.description: Slot index within the style (0 = keystone of the primary tree).

bucket.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the period start (`yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ`), matching the key shape `/ops/stats/matches-over-time` emits so the admin formats both series with one helper. Weeks start on Monday, like Postgres' `date_trunc('week')` — Mongo's `$dateTrunc` would default to Sunday and the two charts would disagree by a day.

matchesInserted.description: Matches newly written in the period. The headline number.

matchesSkipped.description:
Matches the pipeline saw and did not write. Since #1358 that means "already
ingested" only — the off-queue discards moved to their own summary key
(`matchesSkippedWrongQueue`), and with `queue` now sent on the ids call
there should be none. Carried because inserted-alone cannot distinguish "nothing to
do" from "working hard and storing nothing", and those are opposite operational
states.

timelinesUpdated.description: Timelines fetched and attached in the period.

runs.description:
How many ingestion runs started in the period, summary or not. A period with runs
but no inserts is a real signal; a period with no runs at all is a stopped
ingestor.

MatchesIngestedBucket.description: One period's ingestion counters, summed over every run that started in it.

buckets.description:
One bucket per period, oldest first. Periods inside the observed range with no
runs are present with zero counters — a stalled pipeline is exactly what this
chart is for, so its gaps have to be visible rather than absent.

windowDays.description: The effective window in days, after clamping the caller's request.

retentionDays.description:
How far back run history can possibly go: the `process_runs` TTL, in days
(180 by default). Reported so the panel can state the bound instead of drawing
the empty tail beyond it as if the pipeline had ingested nothing then.

earliestRunAtUtc.description:
Start of the oldest run actually seen, or `null` when the
window holds none. Zero-filling starts here rather than at the window's edge:
a period older than the oldest surviving run was not measured, and painting it
as zero would claim an idle pipeline we have no record of.

MatchesIngestedReadModel.description:
Match ingestion throughput over time (#1025) — how many matches the pipeline
     actually ingested per period.

     Deliberately not the same question as /ops/stats/matches-over-time,
which buckets matches.GameStartTimeUtc and therefore describes when the
games were played: a property of the player population, which barely
moves when ingestion stalls and grows in the *past* when a backfill lands. This
one buckets the ingestor's own runs, so it answers "did the pipeline keep up this
week" — the signal the two retention crash-loops (#982, #988) needed and nothing
in the portal carried.

     Sourced from the recorded run summaries in Mongo rather than from
matches.CreatedAtUtc. That column exists and looks tempting, but retention
deletes out-of-window and non-tracked-queue matches, so an old bucket shrinks over
time and the curve rewrites its own history. Deleting a match does not rewrite the
run that ingested it.

position.description: Canonical lane name for lane queues; empty for laneless queues.

filled.description: False when this lane slot has no participant (a gap to highlight).

duplicateChampion.description:
True when this filled slot shares its champion with another slot on the
same team (the duplicate-champion signal), so the UI can mark both.

MatchSlotReadModel.description:
One position slot on a team. For lane queues, string MatchSlotReadModel.Position is one of
the five canonical lanes and bool MatchSlotReadModel.Filled is false when no participant
occupies it. For laneless queues, string MatchSlotReadModel.Position is empty and every
slot is filled (one per participant).

pageSize.description: Number of matches per page (the value the service clamped to).

total.description: Total matches for the player across all pages.

MatchSummariesResponse.description:
Paged response shape. int MatchSummariesResponse.Total is the count of matches
available for the player across all pages — the frontend uses it to
drive a classic page-number pagination control instead of a cursor.

position.description:
Riot team position (TOP/JUNGLE/MIDDLE/BOTTOM/UTILITY). Null when Riot
did not assign one (non-SR modes, remakes) — the frontend then falls
back to raw participant order for the composition columns.

gameName.description: Riot game name (Riot ID prefix). Null when the participant is not a tracked account.

tagLine.description: Riot tag line (Riot ID suffix). Null when the participant is not a tracked account.

isTruncated.description:
True for a game past match retention, read from its truncated seats (#2358): it has no
detail to open, and its CS, kill participation, LP and grade were not kept.

participants.description:
All 10 participants in row order (teamId 100 then teamId 200) so the
frontend can render the versus thumbnails without re-sorting. Includes
the self participant — the UI dedupes by puuid/championId as needed.

MatchSummaryReadModel.description:
One match row in the truemain match history feed
(`GET /truemains/{nameTag}/matches`) — the data needed to render the
collapsed accordion header. Team objective counts are intentionally absent:
they require ingestion changes (see #159) and will be added once those land.

primaryStyleId.description: Riot primary perk style (the keystone's tree).

keystoneId.description:
The actual keystone perk id (slot 0 of the primary tree). Zero when
the perk page failed to ingest cleanly — the frontend falls back to
the tree icon.

cs.description: Sum of lane minions + neutral monsters.

killParticipation.description: Kill participation 0..1 — `(kills + assists) / teamKills`, 0 when the team scored no kills.

items.description: Inventory slots 0..5 (length 6) — the trinket is in int MatchSummarySelfReadModel.TrinketItemId.

roleBoundItemId.description:
Riot's role-bound slot, outside the six inventory slots: a bot laner's boots once the
role quest is done, the other roles' quest reward. 0 when empty or not recorded.

position.description:
The viewing player's Riot team position (TOP/JUNGLE/MIDDLE/BOTTOM/
UTILITY), resolved from the PUUID-matched self participant. Null when
Riot assigned none (non-SR modes, remakes). Exposed here so the frontend
badges the role without re-identifying self by (team, champion) — which
