is ambiguous in queues that allow duplicate champions.

lpDelta.description:
LP gained or lost on this match. Null when the rank snapshots around
the game's window are missing or span a tier/division transition.
Always null in this iteration — derivation lands in a follow-up.

performanceScore.description:
TrueMain performance score for this game, 0–100 — the role-aware blend of
end-of-game stats and the timeline lead curve described in
`Core.Lol.Performance.PerformanceScore`. Computed with the same
scorer and the same inputs as the match detail payload, so the collapsed
row and the expanded panel always agree.

placement.description:
1-based rank of this player's int MatchSummarySelfReadModel.PerformanceScore among the
match's participants (1 = best of all 10).

isMvp.description: True when this participant is the top-scoring player on the winning side.

isAce.description: True when this participant is the top-scoring player on the losing side.

MatchSummarySelfReadModel.description:
The viewing player's slice of the match: championship pick, build,
summoner spells, keystone, KDA / CS, win/loss, and the MVP/ACE flag.

teamId.description: Riot team id (100/200), or a synthetic index for non-standard splits.

playerCount.description: Actual participant rows ingested for this team.

expectedPlayerCount.description:
Players a complete team should carry for this queue, or null when the
queue has no profile (or the team id isn't a standard one). Lets the UI
report "4/5 players" instead of inferring fullness from the slot list,
which also contains unfilled lane gaps and appended unplaced members.

unplacedCount.description:
Members whose `TeamPosition` didn't map onto a canonical lane
(unknown/duplicate position) and were appended after the lane slots.
They exist — the team isn't short — so the UI must report them as
unplaced rather than implying a missing player. Always 0 for laneless
queues.

win.description: Team result, or null when the team has no ingested rows.

MatchTeamReadModel.description: One team's roster, laid out by position with gaps highlighted.

MatchTimeBucket.description: One time bucket of the "matches over time" histogram (`GET /ops/stats/matches-over-time`). Buckets are ordered chronologically and counted by game date (`Match.GameStartTimeUtc`), not ingestion date — game date spreads the distribution meaningfully, whereas `CreatedAtUtc` clusters on the few days the ingestor actually ran. string MatchTimeBucket.Bucket shape depends on the requested granularity: for week/month/year it is the ISO-8601 timestamp of the truncated period start (via date_trunc); for patch it is the normalised "MAJOR.MINOR" form of GameVersion (e.g. 16.4). The frontend formats the per-granularity label.

openConflicts.description: Open known-player account conflicts: the conflict queue's open total.

homonymGroups.description: Homonym groups still holding a pair nobody merged or marked: the homonyms queue's total.

countedAtUtc.description: When the two counts were taken; they are cached a few seconds.

healthStatus.description:
The cockpit verdict — `green` | `amber` | `red` | `unknown` — as the warm
pipeline-health payload holds it. `unknown` as well when no recent evaluation is held:
this read never runs one (see DateTime? NavSummaryReadModel.HealthEvaluatedAtUtc).

healthEvaluatedAtUtc.description:
When that verdict was evaluated; null when no evaluation recent enough is held, which tells an
`unknown` that was measured from one that was not.

NavSummaryReadModel.description:
What the admin sidebar flags on its entries (#2294): the queues waiting for the operator and
the cockpit's verdict, so a pending triage or a red pipeline shows without opening each page.

share.description: Predicted share of the branch for a game in this situation, over the candidates left.

baseShare.description: Share of the branch whatever the game — what the build tree on the champion page shows.

games.description: Games of the branch that took it.

wins.description: Of which won — a measured fact, never the ranking key.

reasons.description: The situations that moved this item most, largest shift first, at most three.

route.description:
The item's components in the order the mains buy them (#2183) — each step's
`Measured` says whether that order was measured or is the recipe's. Empty for an
item with no recipe, or when the item metadata could not be read.

NextItemCandidateReadModel.description: One item the game could complete next.

given.description: True when the caller sent the lane, false when the lane solver guessed it.

NextItemEnemyLaneReadModel.description: An enemy and the lane the situation placed it on.

isBoots.description: True for the boots, whose place in the order is measured apart from the legendaries.

NextItemOrderStepReadModel.description: One step of the build order.

axis.description: The axis, named as the item-context read names it, so the site's wording applies.

bucket.description: `Low` or `High` — the middle of an axis moves a share but has no wording, so it is never a reason.

factor.description: Factor applied to the item's share by this situation (1.4 = forty percent more often).

NextItemReasonReadModel.description: One situation that moved an item: `EnemyMagicDamage` / `High`, and by how much.

patch.description: Optional; the newest patch the champion has a model for when omitted.

items.description: Items held or completed, in completion order when known.

goldLeadAt15.description: Our gold lead over the lane opponent at 15:00, once the game is past it.

NextItemRequest.description: The game state, as posted by the client.

items.description: The items it holds, as the live game reports them — sent for the enemies in game (#1750), never in champion select.

NextItemRequestParticipant.description: Another participant: a champion and, when known, its lane and what it holds.

parentItemId.description: The item the decision follows, 0 at the root of the build.

onTree.description:
False when the build left the mains' tree — it completed an item the mains never take
at that step — and the branch was re-anchored on its latest item that is one.

branchGames.description: Games of the branch behind the base shares.

patchWindow.description: Patches behind the base shares, the served one included.

NextItemSlotReadModel.description: One decision: the branch the game is on and its ranked candidates.

totalMatches.description: Planner estimate of the stored matches (`RawCorpusEstimates`).

totalParticipants.description: Planner estimate of the stored participant rows (`RawCorpusEstimates`).

candidatesByStatus.description:
Main-candidate counts keyed by their `MainCandidateStatus` name
(e.g. "New", "Scored", "Validated"). Every defined status is present, so
the map is stable for the frontend even when a status has zero rows.

matchesLast7Days.description: Planner estimate of the matches played in the last 7 days.

matchesLast30Days.description: Planner estimate of the matches played in the last 30 days.

estimatesUnknownReason.description: Why the estimated figures are null, when they are.

computedAtUtc.description: When this payload was computed — it is served from a short cache.

OverviewReadModel.description:
High-level corpus counters for the admin dashboard landing panel. Nothing here is scoped
     to a single queue or patch (use ChampionStatRow for filtered slices).

     Exact and estimated figures (#2301). The match-side figures —
long? OverviewReadModel.TotalMatches, long? OverviewReadModel.TotalParticipants,
long? OverviewReadModel.MatchesLast7Days, long? OverviewReadModel.MatchesLast30Days — are the planner's
estimates, which the admin prints with ≈: exact counts are full scans of the two
largest tables and ran the endpoint into the API's statement timeout. They are null, with
string? OverviewReadModel.EstimatesUnknownReason, when the estimates could not be read. Every other
figure is exact; int OverviewReadModel.DistinctChampionsWithGames is exact as of the ingestor's
last champion_game_counts recount.

samples.description: Laners counted at this minute (one per participant whose game reached it).

oneOf.description: Cumulative creep score (minions + jungle monsters); null under int PaceBenchmarkResponse.MinSamples.
Cumulative gold earned, starting gold included; null under int PaceBenchmarkResponse.MinSamples.

patches.description: The patches pooled, newest first; empty when nothing has been folded yet.

minSamples.description: The sample a minute needs before its quartiles are served.

tiers.description: Tiers in ladder order (Iron first); a tier with no sample at all is absent.

PaceBenchmarkResponse.description:
The pace benchmark of one position (#1912): for every tier with data, per whole minute,
how many laners were sampled and the quartiles of their cumulative CS and gold earned.
The desktop overlay picks the player's tier locally — the rank it reads from the League
client never leaves the machine — and divides by the minute to show a per-minute rate.

tier.description: The ranked tier, as the `EloBracket` ladder spells it (e.g. `DIAMOND`).

minutes.description: Every minute with at least one sample, ascending.

PatchCoverageDayReadModel.description: One game date's ingestion on a patch.

queueId.description: The ranked queue every count here is scoped to (`MainAnalysis:QueueId`).

minSampleGames.description:
The games floor the public reads apply, echoed from
`ChampionsList:MinSampleGames` rather than re-declared, so this page can
never judge against a bar the site does not enforce.

floorNote.description: The floor stated in words, so the verdict never rests on a bare number.

currentPatch.description:
The patch the public reads resolve to today — the newest one holding aggregate
rows, which is exactly how `ChampionAggregateScopeResolver` picks it. Null
when nothing has been aggregated at all.

verdict.description:
The current patch's verdict, hoisted so the page opens on the answer.
See PatchVerdict PatchCoverageRowReadModel.Verdict.

headline.description: The current patch's verdict in a sentence, with the floor in it.

unknownReason.description:
Why no verdict could be given, when one of the two measurements the page rests on
failed. Set if and only if PatchVerdict PatchCoverageReadModel.Verdict is `unknown` for that reason:
without the coverage rollup, "thin" and "not aggregated" are indistinguishable, and
guessing between them is worse than saying nothing.

participantsNote.description:
How the participant figures are obtained — derived from the match count, not counted
(#2302) — stated beside them so a derived number never reads as a measured one. Null
when no patch was measured.

sourceNote.description: Which tables were read and what that costs, on the panel rather than in a comment.

evaluatedAtUtc.description: When the view was computed. Every age on it is relative to this, not to the browser's clock.

PatchCoverageReadModel.description:
Whether the patches the public surfaces read are actually servable (#1033).

     Every public surface is patch-scoped — the champion directory, the tier list, the
trend charts, the patch diff — and until this view the only way to know that a new
patch was still thin was to browse those pages and eyeball the sample counts. The
question it answers is one sentence long: can the site serve this patch, and if
not, is that because nothing has aggregated it yet or because it genuinely has too
few games? Those two call for opposite reactions, which is why they are separate
verdicts rather than one low number.

patch.description: Normalised "MAJOR.MINOR" patch.

isCurrent.description: True for the patch the public reads currently resolve to.

headline.description: The verdict in a sentence, naming the floor and the bar it was judged against.

matches.description: Matches ingested on this patch, on the scoped queue.

participants.description:
Participants in those matches: the match count times the queue's roster size, derived
rather than counted (#2302) — see string? PatchCoverageReadModel.ParticipantsNote.

firstGameStartUtc.description: Earliest game start on the patch, or null when no match survives retention.

lastGameStartUtc.description: Latest game start on the patch.

daily.description: Matches and participants by game date (UTC), oldest first — how the patch filled.

lines.description:
`(champion, lane)` pairs holding at least one aggregate row on this patch —
the same grain and the same queue filter the champion directory groups by, so the
two can never disagree. Lane-less scope rows are excluded exactly as the ranked
directory excludes them.

linesPastFloor.description: Of those, the ones whose summed games reach int PatchCoverageReadModel.MinSampleGames.

champions.description: Distinct champions with at least one line on this patch.

championsPastFloor.description: Distinct champions with at least one line past the floor.

servableLinesBar.description:
The bar long PatchCoverageRowReadModel.LinesPastFloor was judged against, or null when the patch was
not judged. Derived from the median of the comparable patches, or from
`PatchCoverage:ServableLinesMinimum` when there is no comparable patch.

servableLinesBarNote.description: Where that bar came from, in words — a number with no provenance is not an answer.

belowFloorCount.description: Below-floor lines on their champion's primary lane of this patch — what IReadOnlyList<PatchThinLineReadModel> PatchCoverageRowReadModel.BelowFloor is drawn from, whether or not they all fit in it (#1442). Deliberately not every below-floor line: the off-role tail is short of games because nobody plays the champion there, not because the patch is short of matches, and it is the bulk of the population (all 146 and 194 below-floor lines on the two patches production had filled). That tail is still in the coverage figures — it is long PatchCoverageRowReadModel.Lines minus long PatchCoverageRowReadModel.LinesPastFloor minus this — so a reader can reconcile the two without the list naming lines nobody can act on.

belowFloor.description: Those lines, closest to the floor first, capped by `PatchCoverage:ThinLineLimit`. Ordered that way because the question a thin patch raises is "how far off is it", and the lines about to clear answer it.

folds.description: Per-fold coverage and freshness on this patch.

PatchCoverageRowReadModel.description: One patch's ingestion, aggregate coverage and per-fold state.

measured.description:
False when this patch predates the fold entirely. Raw match payloads are not kept,
so a fold that shipped mid-corpus can never be backfilled (#920 bans): its
rows on older patches are absent by construction,
not missing. A zero there would read as "the fold is broken", which is the one
thing it is not, so every count on such a row is null and
string? PatchFoldCoverageReadModel.NotMeasuredNote says so instead.

firstMeasuredPatch.description: The oldest patch the fold has any row on, or null when it has none at all.

notMeasuredNote.description: Set if and only if bool PatchFoldCoverageReadModel.Measured is false: "not measured before <patch>".

rows.description: Aggregate rows on this patch, or null when the patch is out of the fold's scope.

champions.description: Distinct champions on this patch, or null when out of scope.

lastAggregatedAtUtc.description: Newest write on this patch, or null when there is none.

ageHours.description: Hours since that write, judged against `DataQualityDetectors:AggregationStale*Hours`.

pendingMatches.description:
Matches on this patch the fold has not folded yet, from the per-match flag it
advances. Null for the folds that carry no such flag (builds and mains are
replace-by-scope per account, not per match), where a backlog is not expressible
as a match count.

note.description: What this fold feeds and how to read its numbers.

PatchFoldCoverageReadModel.description:
One aggregation fold's state on one patch: how much it has produced, how fresh that
is, and — for the folds that cannot be backfilled — whether the patch is even in
scope for it.

championId.description: Riot champion id (the admin resolves names from static data).

position.description: Lane the line is scoped to (TOP/JUNGLE/MIDDLE/BOTTOM/UTILITY).

games.description: Games summed across the patch's scope rows for this line.

gamesToFloor.description: Games still missing before the line clears the floor.

PatchThinLineReadModel.description: A `(champion, lane)` line that has games but not enough of them.

PatchVerdict.description: Whether the public reads can serve a patch (#1033).

PerformanceComponentKind.description: The eight graded axes of PerformanceScore.

playRate.description: Share of the account's games on this champion, 0..1.

PersonaAccountEntry.description: One Riot account a source lists for a persona.

gameName.description: The account's current Riot ID — it follows renames, unlike the one the source published.

region.description: `europe`, `americas` or `korea`; null for a platform the site does not expose.

lastPlayedAtUtc.description:
Start of the most recent ranked game TrueMain stored for the account; null when it has none
(never ingested, or every game aged out).

oneOf.description: Latest ranked solo/duo standing; null when unranked.

topChampions.description: Up to three active mains, most played first; empty when never analysed.

status.description:
`linked` — resolved to a tracked account; `pending` — stored, not tracked yet;
`seeded` — stored and queued through the seed intake; `untracked` — stored, on a
platform the pipeline does not ingest, so never seeded; `conflict` — the Riot ID or
its account already belongs to another persona, left untouched and recorded for the admin's
conflict queue; `excluded` — an operator settled a conflict over it against this persona,
unlinked it from this persona, or took it down with a removed persona, so the claim is ignored; `invalid` — malformed, including a placeholder such as
`undefined` for a name or tag.

id.description: The `persona_accounts` row, which the unlink action addresses.

gameName.description: The Riot ID as the source published it.

riotAccountId.description: The tracked account it answers to; null while untracked.

currentGameName.description: The tracked account's current Riot ID (it follows renames); null when untracked.

role.description: `claimant` when this persona claims an account another holds, `owner` when it holds one another claims.

PersonaAdminConflictReadModel.description: An open conflict seen from one persona: which account, and the other persona.

mergedIntoSlug.description: The slug of the persona this one was merged into; null unless merged.

exclusions.description: Riot accounts the persona may no longer claim, newest first.

removedLinks.description: URLs an operator removed, which the sources can no longer add back.

conflicts.description: Open conflicts over the persona's accounts or its claims, most recently seen first.

PersonaAdminDetailReadModel.description:
One known player in full for the admin's edit panel (#2019): every account and link with its row
id and source, what the persona may no longer claim, and its open conflicts.

kind.description: Lowercase kind, as on the public page.

mergedByChannel.description: Same-name personas sharing a social channel merged into their oldest (#2286).

alsoResolved.description: Other open account conflicts those merges settled too.

skipped.description:
Same-name conflicts that changed under the sweep, and same-name channel groups holding a pair
marked as different people: they stay in the queue.

PersonaBatchResponse.description: Response of `POST /ops/personas/batch`: one result per requested persona, in order.

older.description: The one created first: the one a merge keeps by default.

sharedChannels.description: The channels both list. Kinds are lowercase, as on the public page.

PersonaChannelConflictReadModel.description: Two known players listing the same social channel(s), both in full.

total.description: Conflicts matching the search, before paging.

PersonaChannelConflictsReadModel.description:
A page of channel conflicts (#2286): live known players listing the same social channel, the
most channels in common first. Derived from the links, so there is no history: settled ones leave.

gameName.description: The Riot ID as the claiming source published it.

riotAccountId.description: The tracked account it answers to; null while TrueMain does not track it.

currentGameName.description: The tracked account's current Riot ID (it follows renames); null when untracked.

mergedSlug.description: The slug that redirects to string PersonaConflictBulkCandidateReadModel.KeptSlug once merged.

PersonaConflictBulkCandidateReadModel.description: One conflict of the preview and the merge it would get: into the older known player.

oneOf.description: The single resolution's answer, for a resolved one.

PersonaConflictBulkOutcomeReadModel.description:
One conflict of a bulk resolution. PersonaConflictBulkStatus PersonaConflictBulkOutcomeReadModel.Status is `resolved` or `skipped`;
a skip names its PersonaConflictBulkSkipReason? PersonaConflictBulkOutcomeReadModel.Reason: `notFound`, `notOpen` (resolved since, often by an
earlier merge of the same batch), `differingChannel`, `belowFloor` (under the floor, or no shared social channel), or `changed`
(one of the known players was merged or removed since).

PersonaConflictBulkPreviewReadModel.description:
What `POST /ops/personas/conflicts/bulk-resolve` would settle at int PersonaConflictBulkPreviewReadModel.MinScore
(#2295): open conflicts whose two known players share a social channel and list no differing
one, most certain first. int PersonaConflictBulkPreviewReadModel.Eligible counts them all; IReadOnlyList<PersonaConflictBulkCandidateReadModel> PersonaConflictBulkPreviewReadModel.Conflicts holds at
most int PersonaConflictBulkPreviewReadModel.Limit, the batch the operator confirms.

PersonaConflictBulkResolveRequest.description:
Body of `POST /ops/personas/conflicts/bulk-resolve` (#2295): the conflicts the operator
previewed, never a query re-evaluated at click time. The server re-checks each one against
int? PersonaConflictBulkResolveRequest.MinScore before merging it.

PersonaConflictBulkResolveResponse.description: What a bulk resolution did, one outcome per requested conflict in request order.

PersonaConflictBulkStatus.description: What a bulk resolution did with one conflict.

PersonaConflictDetailReadModel.description:
One conflict with both personas in full — every account and link with its source — which is
what the operator reads to decide.

sharedSocial.description: Social kinds (twitch, youtube, x…) whose channel both list.

sharedReferences.description: Reference pages (Leaguepedia, LoLPros, DeepLoL, a website) both list.

differingSocial.description: Social kinds both list, with different channels.

PersonaConflictEvidenceReadModel.description:
The links two personas of a conflict share (#2277). Link kinds are lowercase, as on the public page.
int PersonaConflictEvidenceReadModel.Score: 10 per shared social channel, 3 per shared reference page, −5 per social
kind both list with different channels.

createdAtUtc.description: When the persona was created: the older one is the one a bulk merge keeps (#2295).

PersonaConflictPersonaReadModel.description: One side of a conflict, enough to tell the two apart in the list.

claimant.description: The persona whose source lists the account.

evidence.description: What the two personas' links say about the answer (#2277); the open queue is ordered by it.

PersonaConflictReadModel.description:
One persona claiming a Riot account another persona holds. PersonaConflictStatus PersonaConflictReadModel.Status is
`Open` or `Resolved`; PersonaConflictResolution? PersonaConflictReadModel.Resolution is `Moved`, `Kept`,
`Detached` or `Merged` once resolved.

holderSlug.description: The persona that holds the account now; null when it was detached.

mergedSlug.description: For a merge: the slug that now redirects to string? PersonaConflictResolvedResponse.HolderSlug.

alsoResolved.description: Other open conflicts the action settled too (a merge settles every conflict between the two).

oneOf.description: For `merge` only: `claimant` or `owner`, the persona that stays.

Body of `POST /ops/personas/conflicts/{id}/resolve` (#2253). PersonaConflictAction? PersonaConflictResolveRequest.Action is one of
`move` (the account goes to the claiming persona), `keep` (it stays with its holder),
`detach` (it belongs to neither) or `merge` (the two personas are one person).

PersonaConflictSide.description: A side of a persona conflict: the persona claiming the account, or the one holding it.

PersonaConflictsReadModel.description:
A page of persona account conflicts for the admin queue (#2253), most recently seen first.
long PersonaConflictsReadModel.Total counts the rows matching the filters before paging; long PersonaConflictsReadModel.Open and
long PersonaConflictsReadModel.Resolved count the whole table, for the tab badges.

PersonaConflictStatus.description: Where a PersonaAccountConflict stands. Stored as text (#1251).

slug.description: Lowercase kebab URL key, 1–64 characters of `[a-z0-9-]`, never used before.

PersonaCreateRequest.description:
Body of `POST /ops/personas` (#2019): a known player an operator adds by hand. Everything it
writes carries the source `manual`, and its name is the operator's from then on.

updatedAtUtc.description: The persona's last upsert — the sitemap's `lastmod`.

PersonaDirectoryResponse.description: The known players worth a sitemap entry (`GET /players`, #2018).

accounts.description: For a create or an added account: each account's outcome, as the batch answers it.

PersonaEditedResponse.description: What an admin edit of a known player did (#2019).

PersonaExclusionReason.description: Why an account is excluded from a known player.

personaIds.description: Two or more personas; every pair among them is marked.

key.description: The shared name key (lowercase, without spaces, dots, dashes or underscores).

personas.description: Oldest first: the one a merge keeps by default.

sharedLinks.description:
Links two or more of the group list (#2273) — the same channel, the strongest hint of one person —
as their link key: lowercased, without the scheme, a `www.` or a trailing slash.

distinctPairs.description: Pairs of the group already marked as different people, each as its two persona ids.

mergeIds.description: The personas folded into it; their slugs redirect to it from then on.

keptSlug.description: The persona the others were merged into.

total.description: Groups matching the search, before paging.

A page of homonym groups (#2271): live known players sharing a name, grouped, in name order. A
group whose every pair an operator marked as different people is left out.

trackedAccounts.description: Accounts linked to a tracked account: the ones the public page shows.

openConflicts.description: Open conflicts the persona is part of, as the claimant or as the holder.

disputed.description: True for the account the conflict is about.

kind.description: Lowercase kind, as on the public page.

PersonaOpsReadModel.description: A persona as the admin shows it: every account (tracked or not) and link, each with its source.

pictureUrl.description: The picture of the person's first channel that has one; null when none does.

links.description: Public channels and pages, ordered by kind.

accounts.description: The tracked accounts only, the one played most recently first, then by rank.

PersonaReadModel.description: A known player and every account sources list for them (`GET /players/{slug}`).

PersonaRenameRequest.description: Body of `PATCH /ops/personas/{id}` (#2019): the operator's name for the person.

PersonasPageReadModel.description:
A page of known players for the admin (#2019), most recently updated first. long PersonasPageReadModel.Total
counts the rows matching the filters before paging.

pictureUrl.description: The picture of the person's first channel that has one (#2446); null when none does.

PersonaTagReadModel.description:
The persona a tracked account belongs to, as the leaderboard row and the profile carry it
(#2016): enough to show the person's name and picture and link to `/players/{slug}`.

slug.description: Lowercase kebab URL key (`irelking`), 1–64 characters of `[a-z0-9-]`.

seedMissing.description: Queue an untracked account through the seed intake, so a later upsert can link it.

PersonaUpsertEntry.description:
One known player as a source publishes them. Merging the same person across sources is the
caller's job; the endpoint keys on string? PersonaUpsertEntry.Slug.

created.description: True when this call created the persona, false when it updated an existing one.

error.description: Why the persona was skipped as a whole (malformed slug, name or source); null when it was written.

mergedInto.description:
The slug of the persona this entry fed instead, when an operator merged the requested one into
it (#2253); null otherwise.

removed.description:
True when an operator removed this persona (#2019): the entry was ignored and nothing was
written. Not an error — the source still lists the person, the operator decided otherwise.

steps.description: Every step, in the order a full pass runs them.

PipelineCatalogReadModel.description:
The ingestion pipeline as the admin draws it: every step in execution order, and the two
lanes that partition it. Served from `Data.Pipeline.PipelineCatalog`, the list the
ingestor itself runs.

championDataLagMinutes.description:
Minutes between the newest scoped match and the newest `main_champion_stats`
computation. Null when either side has nothing to measure — notably when no scoped
match exists at all, which before #1031 produced a vast negative number because the
missing timestamp defaulted to `0001-01-01` instead of null.

status.description:
The single verdict: `green` | `amber` | `red` | `unknown`. The
worst of IReadOnlyList<PipelineHealthSignalReadModel> PipelineHealthReadModel.Signals with precedence `red > amber > unknown >
green` — the same vocabulary and the same precedence as the data-quality
detectors, so one dot means one thing across the whole portal.

headline.description:
The verdict as one sentence an operator can act on ("All 5 signals pass", "2
signals are failing"). Never blank.

evaluatedAtUtc.description:
When these signals were measured. Stated on the page because a cockpit that does
not say how old it is invites being read as live when it is a minute stale.

signals.description:
One line per signal, severity-ordered. Each carries the admin route that owns its
detail — this payload deliberately holds no depth of its own.

regionBalance.description:
Per-platform balance (#1153). Informational: it feeds no signal and does not move the
verdict — where the balance becomes a problem is a threshold nobody has set yet.

PipelineHealthReadModel.description:
The operator cockpit payload (#1031): one rolled-up verdict, one line per signal,
     and the raw measurements behind them.

     This is the "is the pipeline healthy right now?" answer in a single response. It
composes the signals that already have their own admin panels — the data-quality
detectors, the per-process run rollup, the disk forecast — rather than re-measuring
them, so a tile can never disagree with the page it links to. The verdict lives here
and not in the frontend because thresholds are a domain decision, and because a
second consumer (alerting) must be able to ask the same question and get the same
answer.

headline.description: The one sentence explaining this signal's current state.

unknownReason.description: Why the signal could not be measured. Set iff DetectorStatus PipelineHealthSignalReadModel.Status is `unknown` — the tile renders this in place instead of a zero that would look healthy. A degraded sub-signal must explain itself, never fail the page.

detailPath.description:
The admin route owning this signal's depth (`/processes`,
`/data-quality`, `/database`). Every tile is a link.

PipelineHealthSignalReadModel.description: One cockpit signal reduced to a verdict, a sentence, and where to go for the detail.

id.description: `fetch` or `aggregate`, as the `lane` filter of the iterations feed accepts.

jobModes.description: The `Job:Mode` values whose passes run this lane.

steps.description: Its step names, in pipeline order.

name.description: The `processName` its runs are recorded under.

jobMode.description: The `Job:Mode` that runs this step alone.

lane.description: The string PipelineLaneReadModel.Id of its lane.

inClaim.description:
Whether the claim allocates to this platform. False for a platform the corpus still holds
but the claim no longer covers (e.g. after narrowing `Platforms:Active`); null when
the claim's platform list is unknown.

accounts.description: Tracked Riot accounts on the platform, any status.

activeMainAccounts.description: Distinct accounts holding at least one active main on the platform.

matchesInWindow.description: Matches of the configured queue ingested on the platform within the window.

matchShare.description: This platform's share of every platform's long PlatformBalanceReadModel.MatchesInWindow; null when the total is 0.

meanCoverageDeficit.description: Mean per-champion coverage deficit in [0, 1] — the allocator's signal. Null when the target is unknown.

championsBelowTarget.description: Champions of the universe below the target on this platform. Null when unknown or the universe is empty.

claimShare.description:
The share of a claim batch the allocator gives this platform from the deficits above:
`(1 + deficit) / Σ(1 + deficit)` over the claim platforms, before the largest-remainder
rounding of an actual batch. Null for a platform outside the claim, or when unknown.

weight.description:
The role profile's nominal weight for this component on the 0..100 scale,
averaged over the sample (a player who switched lanes mid-sample lands
between the two profiles). Zero means the role does not grade it at all.

value.description: Mean 0..1 grade over the games where the component was available. Null when it never was.

games.description: Games the component was available in — the denominator of double? PlayerChampionPerformanceComponent.Value.

PlayerChampionPerformanceComponent.description:
One component of the score averaged over the sample. A component is only
averaged over the games it was actually available in — a game with no
timeline coverage is excluded from the laning average rather than counted as
a zero — so int PlayerChampionPerformanceComponent.Games can be lower than the response's total and is
reported alongside the value.

position.description: The lane the sample was scoped to, or null when every lane was counted.

patch.description: The major.minor patch the sample was scoped to, or null for every patch.

games.description: Ranked solo/duo games on the champion that were actually graded.

minGames.description:
Sample floor: below this many games the averages are suppressed. Exposed
so the frontend can word the empty state with the real number instead of
hardcoding one that drifts.

window.description:
Most recent games the panel ever looks at. The score is a form metric,
not a career one — and the window bounds the read's cost.

averageScore.description: Mean 0–100 score over int PlayerChampionPerformanceResponse.Games. Null below the floor.

bestScore.description: Best single game in the window. Null below the floor.

worstScore.description: Worst single game in the window. Null below the floor.

topOfTeamRate.description:
Share of the graded games the player topped their own side in (MVP on a
win, ACE on a loss), 0..1. Null below the floor.

components.description:
Per-component averages, one entry per component of the model, in the
model's own order. Empty below the floor.

PlayerChampionPerformanceResponse.description:
"How well does this player actually play this champion" — the aggregate of
TrueMain's per-match performance score over the player's recent games on it,
backing `GET /truemains/{nameTag}/champions/{championId}/performance`.

Always a 200 for a known account, even with no usable sample: the
counts are the payload, and a thin sample is reported honestly through
int PlayerChampionPerformanceResponse.Games versus int PlayerChampionPerformanceResponse.MinGames rather than hidden behind a
confident-looking average. Below the floor every score field is
null.

weight.description: Mastery points, or any non-negative weight.

PoolEntry.description: One champion of the player's pool.

oneOf.description:
Effective status, PascalCase: `Success` | `Failed` | `Running` |
     `Abandoned` | `Skipped` | `Cancelled` | `Missing`.

     Effective, not stored: a Running row whose heartbeat has gone stale reads
Abandoned here, via the same ProcessRunStaleness policy
/ops/process-runs applies. Before #1031 this endpoint skipped that step and
lower-cased the name, so a dead run read "running" on the cockpit and
"Abandoned" on the panel the cockpit links to.

lastStartedAtUtc.description: Null when the process has never recorded a run (`Missing`).

lastFinishedAtUtc.description: Null when the process has never recorded a run (`Missing`).

lastSuccessAtUtc.description:
Last successful finish, all-time. Null when the process has never succeeded — which
is a different answer from "succeeded long ago" and must not collapse into one.

consecutiveFailures.description:
Terminal runs since the last success, i.e. the current failure streak. 0 when the
latest run succeeded.

startedAtUtc.description: Earliest `StartedAtUtc` across the iteration's runs — when the pass began.

lastActivityAtUtc.description:
Latest run activity in the iteration: the max `FinishedAtUtc` across its
runs (a still-running run mirrors its start, so this advances as the chain does).

isRunning.description:
True while any run in the iteration is still `Running` — i.e. this is the
pass the pipeline is currently in.

jobMode.description:
The job mode this pass ran, taken from its runs, or null when none of them
recorded one (runs written before #1362 captured it). This is what tells a reader
which lane the pass covered, and therefore which chain it should be judged
against: an iteration that ran the fetch lane is complete, not half-finished.

runs.description: The iteration's runs in pipeline order (by `StartedAtUtc`).

ProcessIterationReadModel.description:
A single pipeline iteration: its id, when it started/last advanced, and the
ordered process runs recorded in it (one per process that ran in the pass).

ProcessIterationsReadModel.description:
One page of pipeline iterations for the admin chain view. Each iteration is
one full pass of the ingestor pipeline (all its processes, in order) grouped
under a shared iteration id, newest iteration first. Only runs stamped with an
iteration id are returned — historical, un-grouped rows have none and are
surfaced through the flat runs feed instead. long ProcessIterationsReadModel.Total is the total
number of iterations (across all pages) so the panel can render a pager.

ProcessRunBaselineReadModel.description:
A successful run measured against the median of the last
int ProcessRunBaselineReadModel.SampleCount successful runs of the same process and job mode.
IReadOnlyDictionary<string, ProcessRunMetricBaselineReadModel> ProcessRunBaselineReadModel.Counters is keyed by the summary's own top-level numeric property
names, verbatim; a counter is absent when too few of those runs recorded it.

ProcessRunMetricBaselineReadModel.description:
One metric of a run against its recent median. double? ProcessRunMetricBaselineReadModel.Deviation is the
relative gap (`1.8` = 180 % above the median), null when the median is zero
and the value is not; bool ProcessRunMetricBaselineReadModel.Flagged says it crossed the policy thresholds,
so the admin never re-derives them.

jobMode.description:
The job mode the pass was running (`Full`, `FetchLane`,
`AggregateLane`, or a single-process mode), or null for runs recorded before
#1362 captured it. Without it a complete fetch-lane pass is indistinguishable from
a full pass that stopped halfway, since the two differ only in which processes
were supposed to run.

oneOf.description:
How this run compares with the recent successful runs of the same process and mode
(#2298), or null when it is not a successful run or that history is too short.

ProcessRunReadModel.description:
A single recorded process run. A
stale-heartbeat `Running` row is reported as "Abandoned" here even though
its stored status is still `Running`. string? ProcessRunReadModel.Error is the stored
failure text (may be null) and JsonElement? ProcessRunReadModel.Summary is the run's JSONB payload
surfaced verbatim, or null when none was recorded.

failureRateInWindow.description:
Fraction of in-window runs that failed, in `[0, 1]`. 0 when no runs
fall inside the window. Derived from real run counts (not a fabricated
metric) so the admin can color failure volume by a meaningful rate rather
than an always-positive absolute count.

ProcessRunRollupReadModel.description:
Per-process summary over the rollup window. The window follows the caller's
`since`: when `since` is omitted the window is unbounded, so
int ProcessRunRollupReadModel.FailureCountInWindow is a true all-time total (≥ any narrower
window) rather than a hidden default. int ProcessRunRollupReadModel.FailureCountInWindow and
int ProcessRunRollupReadModel.RunCountInWindow count only runs whose `StartedAtUtc` falls
inside the window; double ProcessRunRollupReadModel.FailureRateInWindow is their ratio (0 when no
runs fall inside the window). ProcessRunStatus ProcessRunRollupReadModel.LastStatus /
DateTime ProcessRunRollupReadModel.LastRunAtUtc / DateTime? ProcessRunRollupReadModel.LastSuccessAtUtc are unbounded, so an
idle process still reports its real last state (DateTime? ProcessRunRollupReadModel.LastSuccessAtUtc is
null if the process has never succeeded).

ProcessRunsReadModel.description:
Process-run feed for the admin Processes panel: one page of individual runs
(newest first) plus a per-process rollup over the requested window so the
panel can show current health and recent failure volume at a glance.
long ProcessRunsReadModel.Total is the count of all runs matching the active filters
(before paging), so the panel can render a pager; the rollup is computed over
the full filtered set and is unaffected by paging.

ProcessRunStatus.description: Lifecycle of a recorded ingestor process run (ProcessRunDocument).

tagLine.description: Riot tag line (Riot ID suffix). Null when the row was ingested before tag lines were stored.

sampleMatches.description:
How many recent ranked matches int ProfileMainChampionReadModel.Games was counted out of —
the main analysis reads a capped window per account
(`MainAnalysis:MatchesToConsider`), not the player's whole history.
Sent so the profile can name the denominator instead of printing a bare
count that contradicts the champion page's own, differently scoped one
(#1498).

playRate.description: `games / total games on the account` as stored by the main analysis (0..1).

primaryPosition.description: Riot team position string (uppercase, e.g. `MIDDLE`). Empty when no dominant lane.

isSampleRetired.description:
True when the matches these figures were computed from have aged out of
retention, so int ProfileMainChampionReadModel.Games and double ProfileMainChampionReadModel.PlayRate describe a
sample the site no longer holds (#1216). The row is kept on purpose — the
player stays on the leaderboard — but the UI must date it with
DateTime ProfileMainChampionReadModel.MeasuredAtUtc rather than present it as current.

measuredAtUtc.description: When the main analysis last recomputed these figures.

wins.description: Wins this split (nullable when Riot's league response omitted it).

losses.description: Losses this split (nullable when Riot's league response omitted it).

winRate.description:
`wins / (wins + losses)` when both are present, otherwise null.
The frontend hides the winrate label when null instead of rendering
0% or NaN.

oneOf.description: Null when the player has no ranked snapshot yet (unranked or not refreshed).

How devoted the player is to their signature champion (their top main),
0..100 with the full component breakdown. Null when the player has no
champion classified as a main yet — the profile hides the card rather
than showing a zero that would read as "not dedicated".

positions.description:
Account-level position distribution, summed across the player's main
champions. Each entry covers TOP / JUNGLE / MIDDLE / BOTTOM / UTILITY
(Riot strings, uppercase). Always present, possibly empty when the
player has no main champions tracked yet.

oneOf.description: The known player this account belongs to (#2016); null when none.

ProfileReadModel.description:
One truemain profile (`GET /truemains/{nameTag}/profile`) — the
payload behind the profile page. Composes identity (from
`RiotAccount`), latest ranked snapshot (from `RankSnapshot`),
the player's main champions (from `MainChampionStat` where
`IsMain=true`), and an aggregated position breakdown summed across
those mains.

RankHistoryEntryReadModel.description:
One `RankSnapshot` row projected for the chart consumer. At most one
row exists per account per UTC calendar day (see `RankSnapshotWriter`),
so consecutive entries are never duplicates of each other and the gap
between two rows is at least a day, spanning however long the player held
the earlier rank.

RankHistoryReadModel.description:
Rank-history payload behind `GET /truemains/{nameTag}/rank-history`.
Wraps the per-snapshot rows so the response shape can grow (totals,
pagination, queue scoping) without breaking the existing consumer.

rawMatchCount.description:
The planner's live-tuple estimate of `matches` (#2132), not an exact count —
the figure the `/database` panel prints. Null when it could not be read, with
string? RawDataFreshnessReadModel.CountsUnknownReason saying why.

rawParticipantCount.description:
The planner's live-tuple estimate of `matches` (#2132), not an exact count —
the figure the `/database` panel prints. Null when it could not be read, with
string? RawDataFreshnessReadModel.CountsUnknownReason saying why.

countsUnknownReason.description:
Why the two counts are null; null when they were measured. The rest of the block —
the per-platform freshness — does not depend on them.

measuredAtUtc.description:
When these figures were measured. Up to five minutes older than the cockpit's own
evaluation time: the panel is cached, and says so rather than borrowing that timestamp.

windowDays.description: Days covered by IReadOnlyList<PlatformDailyMatchesReadModel> RegionBalanceReadModel.DailyMatches and each platform's window total.

windowStartUtc.description: Start of the first day in the window (UTC midnight).

targetMainsPerChampion.description:
`Coverage:TargetMainsPerChampion` as the Ingestor published it at its last boot.
Null when it has not published one; every deficit is then null too, with
string? RegionBalanceReadModel.CoverageUnknownReason saying why — a deficit computed against a guessed
target would be one the allocator never used.

claimPlatforms.description:
The platforms the match-ingest claim splits its batch across
(`MatchIngestion:Platforms`, which inherits `Platforms:Active`), as the Ingestor
published them. Null when unknown.

configurationCapturedAtUtc.description: When the Ingestor published the two values above. Null when it never has.

coverageUnknownReason.description: Why the coverage columns are null. Set iff int? RegionBalanceReadModel.TargetMainsPerChampion is null.

championUniverse.description:
Champions with an active main on any platform — the denominator of every deficit and
of every below-target share. 0 on a cold start, where the allocator splits evenly.

platforms.description: One row per platform the claim covers or the corpus holds, claim platforms first.

dailyMatches.description:
Matches ingested per platform per UTC day over the window, by ingestion time (not game
time). A day a platform ingested nothing has no row; the client fills the zero.

unknownReason.description:
Set when the panel could not be measured at all; everything else is then empty. The
cockpit renders the reason in place rather than an empty table that reads as "no regions".

RegionBalanceReadModel.description:
Per-platform balance on the health cockpit (#1153): is ingestion spread across the regions
     the way the claim allocator (#1150) means it to be?

     The 82/14/4 imbalance behind #1150 took a manual investigation to find, because the only
per-region view was one run summary's byPlatform split. This answers the question
from one payload: what each region holds, what it ingested over a window and how that
moved day by day, and the coverage deficit the allocator weighs each region's share of the
claim by — computed with the same arithmetic (Core.Coverage.CoverageDeficit) over
the same counts (Data.Queries.ActiveMainCoverageQuery).

binHours.description: The width of one sparkline point, in hours.

slowThresholdMs.description: A route whose p95 is above this is slow; the panel highlights it.

retentionDays.description: The rollup retention the Api is configured with, in days; null when the TTL is disabled.

oldestRetainedUtc.description:
The oldest rollup still stored; null when none is, meaning nothing was ever recorded —
not a quiet window. A window reaching further back was only partly measured.

droppedSinceStart.description:
Requests this Api process measured but could not persist since it started (a failed
write, or more pending routes than the accumulator holds). Zero on a healthy process.

routes.description: Every ops route answered in the window, slowest p95 first.

RequestLatencyReadModel.description:
How long the Api took to answer each ops route over a window (#2307), for the admin
Processes → Performance tab. Measured server-side, from the request reaching the Api to its
answer; the admin proxy's own hop is not in it.

RiotApiBindingLimitReadModel.description:
The app rate-limit window with the smallest sustained-load daily ceiling among
the ones Riot returned (#1035) — the one that binds first under sustained
traffic, not necessarily the one with the highest current-instant usage ratio.

RiotApiCallerUsageReadModel.description: Calls attributed to one caller process (#1035). `"unknown"` when unattributed.

methodRateLimit.description: Freshest `X-Method-Rate-Limit` header seen for this endpoint, or null (#1035).

methodRateLimitCount.description: Freshest `X-Method-Rate-Limit-Count` header seen for this endpoint, or null (#1035).

RiotApiEndpointUsageReadModel.description: Per-endpoint rollup row (ordered by long RiotApiEndpointUsageReadModel.Calls desc).

observedWindowHours.description: Hours of route-keyed history the rates were measured over (at most 7 days).

additionalAccountsHeadroom.description: The binding host's figure: the fewest additional accounts any host can absorb.

bindingRoute.description: The routing host that caps long? RiotApiHeadroomReadModel.AdditionalAccountsHeadroom.

routes.description: Every host with traffic, the binding one first (fewest additional accounts).

RiotApiHeadroomReadModel.description:
Budget-headroom estimate (#1035): "how many more tracked accounts fit". Always
computed over the last 7 days, independent of the panel's selected window, and per
routing host (#1894) — Riot meters each host separately, so each one in
IReadOnlyList<RiotRouteHeadroomReadModel> RiotApiHeadroomReadModel.Routes is measured against its own advertised limit and the one with the
fewest additional accounts, string? RiotApiHeadroomReadModel.BindingRoute, sets
long? RiotApiHeadroomReadModel.AdditionalAccountsHeadroom. bool RiotApiHeadroomReadModel.SufficientData is
`false` — with only double RiotApiHeadroomReadModel.ObservedWindowHours/
double RiotApiHeadroomReadModel.RequiredWindowHours/long RiotApiHeadroomReadModel.TrackedAccounts set — when the
route-keyed history is shorter than the required window, no accounts are tracked, or no
host returned a rate-limit header; the estimate deliberately renders that absent state
instead of extrapolating from a too-thin window.

RiotApiRateLimitReadModel.description:
The most recent rate-limit header snapshot in the window. The app/method
counts are Riot's point-in-time `X-*-Rate-Limit[-Count]` header strings
(e.g. limit `20:1,100:120` / count `3:1,57:120`), surfaced verbatim
for the panel to parse and display.

RiotApiStatusCountReadModel.description: One status-code histogram row. `0` = transport fault (no response).

retries.description: Subset of long RiotApiUsageBucketReadModel.Calls that landed a 429 (#1035).

RiotApiUsageBucketReadModel.description: One time bucket of the call-volume series (chronological).

window.description: The resolved window key echoed back: `1h` / `24h` / `7d` / `30d`.

sinceUtc.description: Lower time bound the metrics were aggregated from (UTC).

errorRate.description: Errors / total calls in [0, 1]; 0 when there were no calls.

avgLatencyMs.description: Mean per-attempt round-trip latency in milliseconds.

oneOf.description: Latest rate-limit header snapshot in the window, or null when none was seen.

callerBreakdown.description: Calls attributed to each caller process, ordered by `Calls` descending (#1035).

headroom.description: Budget-headroom estimate, always computed over the last 7 days (#1035).

RiotApiUsageReadModel.description:
Riot API usage metrics over a relative window for the admin
`/ops/riot-usage` panel (#93): totals, a per-endpoint breakdown, a
status-code histogram, a bucketed call-volume series, and the most recent
rate-limit header snapshot. Sourced from the per-minute
`riot_api_call_rollups` Mongo collection.

coverageStartUtc.description:
Where the rates are measured from: DateTime RiotQuotaReadModel.SinceUtc, or the oldest
route-keyed rollup when the retention or the #1458 cutover ends inside the window
(now, with double RiotQuotaReadModel.CoveredHours at zero, when there is none yet). Every
per-host rate divides by double RiotQuotaReadModel.CoveredHours, never by the nominal window.

retentionDays.description: The rollup retention the API is configured with, in days; null when the TTL is disabled.

oldestRetainedUtc.description: The oldest rollup still stored; null when the collection is empty.

routes.description: Regional hosts first, then platform hosts, each by calls descending.

RiotQuotaReadModel.description:
Riot quota utilisation for the admin Riot API panel (#1458): one row per routing host
— Riot keeps one app budget per host — with its measured call rate against the limit
that host advertised, its 429 rate and who spent it, plus the duty cycle of each
ingestor lane over the same window.

RiotRouteConsumerReadModel.description: One caller × endpoint spending a host's budget. double RiotRouteConsumerReadModel.Share is of the host's calls.

kind.description: `regional` or `platform` — two budget families, never added.

additionalAccountsHeadroom.description: Floor of the host's spare capacity divided by its per-account cost.

RiotRouteHeadroomReadModel.description:
One routing host's headroom (#1894): its calls/day over the covered span, that cost per
tracked account, and what is left under the binding window of the limit it advertised.
RiotApiBindingLimitReadModel? RiotRouteHeadroomReadModel.BindingLimit, double? RiotRouteHeadroomReadModel.SpareCallsPerDay and
long? RiotRouteHeadroomReadModel.AdditionalAccountsHeadroom are null when the host returned no parseable
`X-App-Rate-Limit` header.

calls.description: Every physical attempt, 429s included — a rejected request still counted.

rateLimitedRate.description: 429s / calls in [0, 1]; null when there were no calls.

callsPerMinute.description: Calls per minute averaged over the covered span.

activeMinuteShare.description: Share of the covered span's minutes with at least one call to this host.

oneOf.description: The advertised window with the lowest sustained ceiling (same rule as the headroom estimate).

utilisation.description: Calls over the covered span / what the binding limit allows over it.

currentUtilisation.description:
The freshest `X-App-Rate-Limit-Count` on the binding window divided by its
limit — the instantaneous fill of the host's budget at DateTime? RiotRouteQuotaReadModel.ObservedAtUtc.

RiotRouteQuotaReadModel.description:
One routing host's budget. string RiotRouteQuotaReadModel.Kind is `regional` (americas, europe,
asia, sea — account-v1 and match-v5), `platform` (euw1, na1, kr… — summoner,
league, mastery) or `unknown`. The utilisation fields are null when the host
returned no parseable `X-App-Rate-Limit` in the window: without the advertised
limit there is nothing to divide by.

RouteLatencyPointReadModel.description: One sparkline point; double? RouteLatencyPointReadModel.P95Ms is null when the route was not called in the bin.

p50Ms.description: Median duration, estimated from the bucket counts.

p95Ms.description: 95th percentile, estimated from the bucket counts; never above double RouteLatencyReadModel.MaxMs.

timeouts.description: Requests abandoned by the client, cancelled or timed out.

series.description: One point per int RequestLatencyReadModel.BinHours across the whole window, oldest first.

accountCount.description: The person's tracked accounts — the ones their page lists. Never 0: a person with none is not returned.

pictureUrl.description: The picture of the person's first channel that has one; null when none does.

oneOf.description: The best-ranked tracked account's rank; null when it is unranked.

SearchPlayerReadModel.description: A known player in the search results, linking to `/players/{slug}`.

players.description:
Known players whose name matches the term (#2018), best first, at most five. Empty when the
query carries a tag — a `Name#TAG` asks for one account, not a person.

SearchResponse.description:
Response for the truemain search endpoint (`GET /truemains/search`):
a short, ranked list of accounts whose `GameName` matches the query,
used to power the name/tag lookup that links straight to a profile page.
The population mirrors the leaderboard's (ranked mains on the exposed
regions) so search is a faster way into the same list, not a different one.

region.description: One of `europe`, `americas`, `korea`. Mirrors the leaderboard's region slug.

oneOf.description:
Latest ranked cell (tier/division/LP) for the account, so the dropdown
can show rank next to the name. Null when the account has no rank
snapshot yet — which, given the ranked gate on the population, only
happens transiently between discovery and the first rank sync.

topChampionIds.description:
Up to 3 most-played champion ids (descending play rate), same slice
the leaderboard row shows, so the dropdown can render the player's
truemained champions at a glance. Empty when no main-champion analysis
has run yet.

oneOf.description:
Primary + secondary lane from position share across the player's mains
(same derivation as the leaderboard, via `MainPositions`). Null
when no main-champion analysis has run.

SeedRequestAcceptedResponse.description:
202 body for an accepted seed request: the row id, its current status, and whether it was
created by this call. bool SeedRequestAcceptedResponse.Created is `true` for a freshly-inserted request
and `false` when an existing unprocessed request was returned instead (idempotency) —
letting the caller tell a brand-new seed apart from an "already seeded" hit.

SeedRequestReadModel.description:
A single "seed by Riot ID" request as surfaced to the admin panel. The API
records the row at `Pending`; the Ingestor's ManualSeedProcess resolves
the Riot ID, upserts the account, and stamps the terminal state.
SeedRequestStatus SeedRequestReadModel.Status is the `SeedRequestStatus` name
("Pending"/"Resolving"/"Ingested"/"Failed"). string? SeedRequestReadModel.Error carries the
failure detail when SeedRequestStatus SeedRequestReadModel.Status is "Failed" (else null);
string? SeedRequestReadModel.ResolvedPuuid and Guid? SeedRequestReadModel.ResolvedRiotAccountId are
populated once ingested.

SeedRequestsReadModel.description:
A page of seed requests for the admin intake list, newest-first.
    long SeedRequestsReadModel.Total counts every row matching the active filters, before
    paging, so the panel can render a pager and say how much of the queue is left.
    Shaped like CandidatesReadModel on purpose: the two lists sit on the
same page and answer the same kind of question, so they page identically
(#1166).

SeedRequestStatus.description:
Lifecycle of a seed request (SeedRequestDocument). SeedRequestStatus.Pending and
SeedRequestStatus.Resolving are the unprocessed states the idempotency check and
the Ingestor's claim scan look at; SeedRequestStatus.Ingested and
SeedRequestStatus.Failed are terminal. Stored as the enum name (a string) so the
document is human-readable in the shell.

engine.description:
Which engine the object belongs to: `postgres` or `mongo` (#1023). A
table and a collection are not the same kind of object, and two of them share a
name (`process_runs`, `seed_requests`), so the list says which is
which rather than merging them into one undifferentiated column.

tableName.description: The Postgres table name, or the Mongo collection name.

rowEstimate.description:
Planner live-tuple estimate for Postgres (0 before the first ANALYZE); an exact
document count for Mongo, which reports one cheaply.

TableStatRow.description:
Physical storage footprint of a single table in the `public` schema,
sourced from `pg_catalog`. long TableStatRow.RowEstimate is the planner's
live-tuple estimate (`pg_stat_user_tables.n_live_tup`), not an exact count,
and can read 0 until the table is analysed/vacuumed. Byte figures are
`pg_total_relation_size` (total) = `pg_relation_size` (table heap) +
`pg_indexes_size` (indexes) + TOAST.

firstItemId.description:
First completed item (`BuildItem0`) of the dominant
    ChampionDimBuild for this slice.

primaryKeystoneId.description: Primary keystone of the rune page tied to the dominant build.

secondaryStyleId.description:
Secondary tree (style) ID — frontend resolves the tree icon
    via the shared rune-tree static payload.

itemPath.description:
Raw item progression of the top `ChampionDimBuild`,
    `BuildItem0`..`BuildItem6` stripped of zero slots. The most
    common exact sequence rather than a probabilistic "consensus path" —
    cheap to compute over the directory and still meaningful at a glance.

TopBuildReadModel.description:
Summary of the most-played build for a `(champion, position)` pair on
the active patch. Surfaces just enough for the directory list to render
the keystone, secondary tree, and item sequence inline — full build /
runes / variations remain on `GET /champions/{id}`.

key.description:
Stable cell identity: `yyyy-MM-dd` of the UTC day on a calendar
window, the match id on the day window. Unique within the series, so the
client can key on it.

startUtc.description:
Start of what the cell covers: 00:00 UTC of its day, or the game's start
instant. Never null — every window this endpoint emits is dated.

games.description: Games in the cell. `0` is a real answer: an idle day.

winRate.description:
Win rate in the cell, or `null` when int TruemainActivityBucketReadModel.Games
is 0. This is the wire-level distinction between "played and lost
everything" (0) and "did not play" (null); the two must not render alike.

championId.description:
Champion played, on the day window only — a per-game cell is one game, so
it has exactly one. `null` on a calendar cell, which can
span several champions.

TruemainActivityBucketReadModel.description:
One cell of the activity grid: a UTC day on the patch and week windows, a
single game on the day window.

month.description:
One cell per UTC day over the last thirty days, clamped to the oldest game
retention still holds.

patch.description:
One cell per UTC day of the current patch, from the day the patch's first
game was played through today. The default view.

week.description: One cell per UTC day over the last seven days, today included.

day.description: One cell per game played on the current UTC day; empty on a rest day.

coverageFromUtc.description:
Start of the window the series speaks for, or `null` when
it holds no cell at all. Read off the emitted cells rather than computed a
second time, so the claim and the squares behind it cannot drift.

coverageToUtc.description: End of the window the series speaks for; see DateTime? TruemainActivitySeriesReadModel.CoverageFromUtc.

buckets.description: The cells, oldest first. The two calendar windows emit a cell for every day they span, including the days with no games — an idle day is a fact worth drawing, and the run of them between two sessions is what makes a busy stretch legible.

winRate.description:
Win rate across the window, or `null` when
int TruemainActivitySeriesReadModel.Games is 0. Never 0 for an empty window — "measured at 0%"
and "nothing measured" are different facts.

TruemainActivitySeriesReadModel.description: One window of the activity grid.

riotId.description: The Riot ID as TrueMain stores it, `Name#TAG`; match it case-insensitively.

nameTag.description: The `{gameName}-{tagLine}` slug of the player's profile.

championId.description: The champion they were asked with, which they main.

championMatches.description: Recent ranked games on the champion.

totalMatches.description: Recent ranked games the share is measured over (capped by main analysis).

isOtp.description: A one-trick on the champion: the same flag as the OTP badge.

masteryPoints.description: Riot champion-mastery points on the champion; null until read.

dedication.description: The Truemain score on this champion, 0..100 (double DedicationReadModel.Score).

TruemainLookupEntryReadModel.description:
One player found to be a true main of the champion they were asked with:
the figures the desktop app's mark explains itself with, all read off the
same `main_champion_stats` row the leaderboard admits them on.

TruemainLookupResponse.description:
Answer of `GET /truemains/lookup` (#1910): of the players asked about,
the ones who are true mains of the champion they were asked with. A player
who is not is simply absent, so the response says nothing about anyone else.
